description: Use when a paper claims a quantitative speedup (e.g. '59x faster') and you need to independently verify runtimes by re-executing the tool on the deposited benchmark data with the paper's parameters.

name: conditional-randomization-test-implementation
description: Use when testing conditional independence between gene expression features and a response (protein counts, synthetic y, perturbation readouts) in single-cell data with a requirement for calibrated FDR control without linearity or Gaussian-response assumptions.

name: confounder-adjusted-conditional-independence-testing
description: Use when single-cell count data (scanpy AnnData with raw counts, response Y in obsm) must be tested for feature–response dependencies while adjusting for technical/biological nuisance factors such as batch, sequencing depth, or cell cycle.

name: consensus-clustering-baseline-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether a new consensus/ensemble clustering method for scRNAseq outperforms existing individual algorithms (Seurat-Louvain, Seurat-SLC, CHOIR, RACEID, SC3, Spectrum, scSHC) and the SAME-clustering ensemble, using ARI/NMI against known cell-type labels.

name: consensus-clustering-ensemble-execution
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data require a consensus cell-type clustering that ensembles multiple algorithms (e.g., Seurat-Louvain, SC3, Spectrum, scSHC) instead of trusting one method's assignments.

name: consensus-nmf-factorization
description: Use when performing unbiased multi-resolution program discovery within a single modality (bulk RNA-Seq, MS proteomics, or snRNA-Seq) prior to cross-dataset integration, starting from over-dispersed feature sets.

name: constraint-optimization-validation-against-reference
description: Use when designing a multi-omics experiment that needs an optimal number of replicates per omic under minimum power, average power, FDR, effect size and cost constraints, and the optimization result must be cross-checked against the package reference.

name: context-specific-network-inference
description: Use when a seed set of omic-hits (e.g., mutated or phosphoproteomic hits from 105 CPTAC breast cancer tumors) must be converted into a context-specific subnetwork over a reference interactome such as HIPPIE or ConsensusPathDB.

name: conventional-pathway-layout-preservation
description: Use when visualizing KEGG pathway networks (KGML) where biological interpretability of the conventional map layout matters, e.g. when comparing how automated layout algorithms obscure cyclic structures like the TCA cycle.

name: cooltools-contact-map-analysis
description: Use when ensemble single-cell Hi-C contact maps (e.g. sci-L3-Hi-C cool files) must be compared to a bulk Hi-C map for A/B compartment recapitulation, or when cis eigenvectors need phasing against a histone-mark track.

name: copy-number-focal-amplification-detection
description: Use when per-sample TCGA copy-number segment data are available alongside iMLGAM risk scores and the goal is to identify focal amplifications (e.g. 9p24.1 CD274/PDCD1LG2) and test their enrichment in a defined tumor subgroup.

name: correlation-matrix-handling-dependent-tests
description: Use when combining p-values or z-scores whose tests are not independent and metacp therefore needs a user-supplied correlation matrix, a weight matrix, or its default correlation computed from the observations.

name: correlation-matrix-pvalue-combination
description: Use when input is a text file of n rows × k columns of p-values or z-scores whose tests are not independent and a correlation matrix is available or can be estimated, and per-row combined p-values are needed.

name: correlation-matrix-specified-meta-analysis
description: Use when the input is a text file of n rows x k columns of p-values or z-scores from tests that are not independent (e.g. correlated SNPs in a GWAS) and a correlation matrix can be provided or derived.

name: correlation-regression-coefficient-matrix-computation
description: Use when preparing a normalized gene/variable expression matrix (genes as row identifiers, samples as columns, e.g. normalizedCounts_coding.tsv) for co-expression clustering, and you need correlation plus regression-slope matrices as input to spectral clustering.

name: correlation-significance-testing
description: Use when you have paired per-method score vectors (e.g. accuracy scores from the 49-method simulation benchmark) computed separately on SRT and scRNA-seq reference datasets, and you need to test their linear agreement.

name: corum-complex-tissue-relevance-scoring
description: Use when building tissue-specific complex prior probabilities (P_complex_initial) for Protrec2 — e.g. when curated complex records in updated_tissue_complex_.csv must be scored across the 27 supported tissues before Bayesian inference.

name: cosine-similarity-network-comparison
description: Use when multiple sample-specific networks (e.g. pyPARAGON subnetworks per tumor) must be compared and grouped, via functional-module annotation profiles such as over-represented biological processes.

name: cost-constrained-sample-size-optimization
description: Use when decision support for selecting the optimal number of replicates per omic in a multi-omics experimental design when per-technology power targets, an average power threshold, an FDR level and platform costs must be balanced simultaneously.

name: count-based-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when RNA-seq reads (or their Salmon quantification output) must be tested for differential expression between defined groups, e.g. the simulated disease vs normal samples in the eduomics RNA subworkflow.

name: count-data-dispersion-estimation
description: Use when pilot multi-omic count matrices (preprocessed, batch-effect-free) are available and per-feature dispersion/variability parameters must be estimated to feed downstream sample-size/power estimation (e.g., optimalRep in MultiPower).

name: count-matrix-log-transformation
description: Use when simulated count matrices from MOSim (mosim) or sc_mosim must be transformed before clustering, PCA, or benchmarking of clustering tools, as the MOSim methods specify log(x + 1) on count data.

name: crispr-screen-gene-prioritization
description: Use when multiple published CRISPR/Cas9 screening cohorts with immune-competent vs immune-deficient conditions are available and the goal is a consensus gene ranking tied to iMLGAM-score prognostic markers.

name: cross-cancer-omics-panel-integration
description: Use when you need to render a pan-cancer multi-omics AnnotatedHeatmap from fold-change and p/q-value matrices with significance stars and annotation tracks, e.g. epigenetic-marker vs. gene-expression associations across TCGA cancer panels.

name: cross-cohort-program-network-integration
description: Use when two or more expression datasets (bulk/single-cell/spatial, possibly with mismatched features and no shared sample IDs) must be integrated at the program level and annotations such as transcriptional subtypes propagated from a reference cohort to a new cohort.

name: cross-cohort-proteomics-validation
description: Use when recovered/predicted missing proteins from a discovery proteomics run (e.g. Protrec2 output on six matched lung tumor-normal pairs from PXD000603) need independent confirmation in a public cohort such as CPTAC before being reported.

name: cross-cohort-zscore-normalization
description: Use when sgRNA read logFCs from several independent CRISPR screening cohorts (e.g. Freeman, Kearney, Manguso, Pan, Patel, Vredevoogd, Lawson) must be combined into a single consensus gene ranking.

name: cross-dataset-hic-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking per-cell informative chromatin interaction counts across single-cell Hi-C modalities, or when harmonizing published valid-pair datasets (e.g. GSM2254217, GSE174226) under identical distance and deduplication filters.

name: cross-language-single-cell-exchange-validation
description: Use when a multimodal single-cell dataset stored as a .h5mu file (e.g. PBMC RNA+ATAC) must be loaded in R from a Python/Julia workflow, and cross-language fidelity of modalities and cell barcodes must be validated.

name: cross-layer-expression-heatmap-generation
description: Use when you have simulated (or real) count matrices for several omic layers plus group/time-point design settings, and you need per-group visualizations whose rows/columns align across layers to inspect regulatory patterns.

name: cross-method-module-annotation-verification
description: Use when you have gene-module assignment tables from two co-expression methods (e.g., SGCRNA spectral clusters and WGCNA brown4/grey modules) plus a paper's reported GO term associations, and you need to independently rerun GO enrichment per module and record agreement.

name: cross-method-module-count-comparison
description: Use when comparing module granularity of co-expression methods (SGCRNA vs WGCNA/hdWGCNA) on the same gene or genus-level count matrix, e.g. bulk RNA-Seq, Visium spatial, or 16S amplicon data.

name: cross-method-timing-statistics-aggregation
description: Use when you need to quantify and compare the computational cost of two analysis pipelines (e.g., SGCRNA's spectral-clustering eigenvector computation vs WGCNA) on an identical transcriptomic dataset, with replicated timed runs and statistical aggregation.

name: cross-modal-community-composition-analysis
description: Use when an anchor network of molecular programs has been integrated across datasets/modalities (e.g. from a thresholded Pearson correlation matrix) and you need its community partition and the modality composition of each community.

name: cross-modality-cell-assignment-agreement-evaluation
description: Use when a joint single-cell assay (e.g. sci-L3-RNA/ATAC) yields count matrices per modality plus per-cell SNV genotype calls, and you must quantify whether each modality alone distinguishes cell types correctly.

name: cross-modality-program-usage-integration
description: Use when per-patient program/community usage values exist in ≥2 -omics modalities (e.g., RNA and protein in CPTAC GBM) and the goal is to test whether combined cross-modality usage reveals clinical (survival) associations.

name: cross-package-numerical-validation
description: Use when a new or reimplemented statistical method (e.g., p-value combination in metacp) must be verified against an established reference package before trust is placed in its numerical output.

name: cross-technology-segmentation-benchmarking
description: Use when decision support for choosing between open-source (Sopa/Baysor) and proprietary (Vizgen/10X Genomics) segmentation when raw imaging-based spatial transcriptomics data with transcripts plus a vendor segmentation prior is available and cell-type resolution must be compared.

name: cross-validation-benchmark-of-network-methods
description: Use when comparing multiple network inference tools (e.g., pyPARAGON vs PL, OI2, DOMINO) on identical seed gene sets and a shared reference interactome, with known drivers as the validation ground truth.

name: cross-version-performance-comparison
description: Use when a paper claims a rewritten tool is faster than its predecessor (e.g. Scoary2 vs Scoary) and you must reproduce the reported speedup (~30x) and the asymptotic runtime scaling on synthetic data.

name: crt-pvalue-computation-with-generative-models
description: Use when raw single-cell counts in a scanpy AnnData need calibrated FDR-controlled tests of conditional dependence between genes and response variables (e.g., protein levels in obsm), especially for nonlinear relationships.

name: cutsite-count-aggregation
description: Use when benchmarking Hi-C protocol choice by restriction motif frequency — e.g. reproducing reported cut-site totals (MboI ~7M, AluI 13M, combination ~30M) on hs37d5 or comparing cutter frequency across single-cell Hi-C methods.

name: cytolytic-activity-quantification
description: Use when a bulk RNA-seq cohort (e.g., TCGA) has been stratified by a score such as iMLGAM riskscore and you need per-sample cytolytic activity alongside other immune metrics (leukocyte/lymphocyte/TIL fractions, CD8+ T cell abundance) to compare groups.

name: cytoscape-network-automation-via-rcy3
description: Use when the goal is to reproduce or redraw a multi-layered trans-omic network (e.g., KEGG rno04910 over two rno01100 layers, or the five-layer mmu04910/mmu01100 glucose-response network) automatically from tabular connectivity data rather than manual Cytoscape editing.

name: cytoscape-network-layout-comparison
description: Use when you need to verify that an algorithmically generated network layout (e.g. degree-sorted circle or CoSE) retains the conventional pathway-map layout biologists rely on to locate metabolites and enzymes.

name: cytoscape-subnetwork-export
description: Use when an RWR_LOE ranking over a multiplex network must be visualized: you have seed genes, a ranked gene output, and need the top-N (e.g., 50) highest-ranked nodes extracted and sent to Cytoscape for exploration.

name: danaher-infiltration-score-computation
description: Use when a TCGA bulk RNA-seq cohort must be stratified by iMLGAM 'riskscore' (from predict(ga_fit, ...)) and immune infiltration — Danaher scores, leukocyte/lymphocyte/TIL fractions, CD8+ T cells — contrasted between score groups.

name: dataset-pair-correlation-thresholding
description: Use when integrating cNMF-derived molecular programs across cohorts or -omics modalities with incomplete feature overlap, and you need dataset-pair-specific correlation thresholds to select highly correlated program pairs as anchors.

name: deep-graph-infomax-contrastive-learning
description: Use when building self-supervised spot-level latent representations from spatial transcriptomics data where a spot-by-gene matrix and a spatial adjacency matrix are available, and you need negatives for a contrastive GCN objective without image data.

name: delaunay-graph-border-extraction
description: Use when cell-level spatial data has been grouped into niches (e.g., via STAGATE) and you need contiguous polygon shapes per niche to compute geometric properties like area, perimeter, and roundness.

name: delaunay-spatial-neighbor-graph-construction
description: Use when you have a segmented SpatialData object with cell boundaries, cell-type labels, and niche assignments, and you need cell-cell adjacency to quantify colocalization via hop distances.

name: dependent-p-values-method-classification
description: Use when choosing or documenting which p-value combination method fits a set of independent or correlated test statistics (e.g. SNPs from a GWAS, gene/probe sets from transcriptomics) and whether correlation or weight matrices must be supplied.

name: deterministic-attractor-analysis
description: Use when a curated biomolecular regulatory network must be iterated to its stable attractor states under normal or personalized input conditions to quantify cell fate outcome probabilities.

name: differential-expression-cutoff-classification
description: Use when a task requires thresholding differential-expression results into up/down/neutral classes and annotating per-panel counts on volcano/scatterplot facets from DE tables, matrices+metadata, or MultiAssayExperiment objects.

name: differential-expression-go-enrichment
description: Use when a Leiden (or equivalent) clustering over an integrated embedding — e.g. SSGATE's 30-dim joint transcriptome-proteome output — needs functional interpretation via per-cluster marker genes and GO term annotation.

name: differential-expression-overlap-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq simulation methods on their ability to regenerate ground-truth differential expression between cell groups, or when reproducing the paper's DEG functionality scores (e.g., Lun = 0.90) from simmethods/simpipe outputs.

name: differential-expression-significance-thresholding
description: Use when you have a precomputed DE table, expression/count matrix with metadata, or a MultiAssayExperiment object and need faceted volcano plots (log2 fold-change vs -log10(p-value)) with thresholded significance classification.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when salmon-quantified transcript counts from simulated RNA-seq reads (Polyester-generated FASTQ with a known injected DE pattern) must be analyzed with DESeq2 and GO enrichment validated for teaching workflows.

name: differential-rna-editing-analysis
description: Use when you have per-sample RNA editing event tables (e.g. _Edit__DATA.tsv from Mapit callediting) for an RBP treatment and matched control, and need to identify which transcripts are significant RBP binding targets.

name: diffusion-pseudotime-baseline-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when single-cell data spans a gradual biological transition (e.g. EMT) and you need a continuous pseudotime baseline to compare against DNN training-dynamics confidence scores or marker expression trends.

name: disease-associated-gene-ranking
description: Use when you have single-cell data (e.g. an AnnData object such as mSTZ β cells) already annotated and carrying per-cell confidence scores, and you want to identify genes whose expression is positively or negatively correlated with a disease/annotation signal.

name: disease-state-characterization-in-beta-cells
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data from disease/treatment conditions (e.g. mSTZ β cells annotated by condition) must be partitioned into disease-related vs. healthy-like cell states using training-dynamics scores rather than expression alone.

name: dna-read-simulation-with-variant-injection
description: Use when building educational genomic datasets where students must practice variant calling against data with known injected pathogenic variants, or when validating that simulated reads reproduce a specific ClinVar variant.

name: dna-variant-calling-from-simulated-reads
description: Use when you have simulated paired-end DNA FASTQ files with a known injected ClinVar pathogenic variant (disease vs normal) and must verify the variant is recoverable by variant calling before using the data for teaching variant-calling workflows.

name: dockerized-r-benchmark-execution
description: Use when benchmarking the 49 simmethods simulation methods for scRNA-seq/SRT data and you need identical dependency environments across runs, or when reproducing per-method execution-error rates.

name: dockerized-r-environment-orchestration
description: Use when local installation of simmethods/simpipe (and tislingshot) is impractical due to dependency conflicts, and a reproducible containerized R setup is needed to execute scRNA-seq/SRT simulations.

name: drawing-time-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to benchmark how rendering/scalability of an automated network visualization pipeline (e.g., transomics2cytoscape with Cytoscape) changes as the number of stacked network layers increases.

name: dropout-noise-injection
description: Use when benchmarking ST integration methods (e.g. stImage vs MUSE) on synthetic data that must include controlled transcriptomic missingness, or when reconstructing simulated ST datasets with distinct/ambiguous spatial patterns across 4, 6, 8, or 10 clusters.

name: drug-activity-score-computation
description: Use when a personalized cancer model (CanSeer-style) needs quantitative drug effect scores from tissue mean IC50 values plus a patient's normalized RNA-seq expression of drug-target genes with known oncogene/TSG roles.

name: drug-approval-status-annotation
description: Use when you have a list of predicted monotherapies or drug combinations from an in silico therapeutic prioritization (e.g. CanSeer drug-score output) and need to classify each entry by FDA approval status, literature support, and novelty.

name: drug-combination-categorization
description: Use when you have a list of predicted single drugs and drug combinations from CanSeer (e.g., from Supplementary Data) and need to stratify them by FDA approval status, prior literature support, repositioning status, or novelty.

name: dsb-background-denoising
description: Use when CITE-seq 'Antibody capture' ADT counts need background-corrected normalisation before cell-type definition or gating-like downstream analysis, and both filtered and raw feature-barcode matrices are available.

name: duplicate-read-pair-marking-and-classification
description: Use when processing barcode-annotated, bwa-aligned single-cell Hi-C pairsam/pair files and you need duplicate marking (markasdup), valid-pair class filtering (UU, UR, RU), and per-depth-class duplicate/retention statistics.

name: dynamical-network-analysis-of-biomolecular-models
description: Use when a validated biomolecular regulatory network model needs to be annotated with sample-specific RNA-seq (and/or genetic alteration) data and simulated via dynamical analysis to quantify cell fate propensities for treatment-response assessment.

name: ec-to-kegg-reaction-id-mapping
description: Use when an inter-layer interaction TSV references enzymes by EC numbers (e.g. 2.7.1.1 in column 6) but the downstream pathway layer uses KEGG reaction IDs (rn:R#####), and both edge types must attach to the same KEGG enzyme layer.

name: edge-flux-prioritization
description: Use when you have a flux-scored GGN from the Personalized PageRank and flux-calculation step and must reconstruct a context-specific subnetwork by thresholding edges with the tau x F criterion.

name: edge-midpoint-node-insertion
description: Use when you have a trans-omic interaction TSV whose rows connect nodes in different stacked pathway layers of a Cytoscape 2.5D network and need those inter-layer edges drawn programmatically.

name: edit-cluster-delineation-from-per-site-calls
description: Use when per-nucleotide RNA editing calls (SAILOR BED sites from hADAR2dd A-to-G and rAPOBEC1 C-to-U deamination) must be aggregated into reproducible paired edit clusters marking high-confidence RBP-binding regions.

name: effect-size-estimation-cohens-d
description: Use when a pilot multi-omic count matrix is available and MultiPower's optimalRep/MultiPower functions require input parameters (variability, effect size, dispersion percentiles) derived from per-feature effect sizes.

name: effect-size-tradeoff-curve-interpretation
description: Use when a MultiPower optimization run on pilot multi-omics data (e.g. STATegra miRNA-seq, RNA-seq, DNase-seq, metabolomics) needs a post-hoc analysis of how many replicates per group achieve a target detectable Cohen's d, especially when equalSize=FALSE allows unequal per-omic sizes at equal cost.

name: effective-number-of-tests-adjustment
description: Use when combining dependent p-values from correlated tests (e.g., SNPs in LD, correlated gene probes) and Bonferroni with the raw number of tests would over-correct; a correlation matrix for the test statistics is available or estimable.

name: effective-number-of-tests-eigenvalue-estimation
description: Use when combining dependent p-values where a correlation matrix is available and you want a Bonferroni-style correction that replaces the raw number of tests with an eigenvalue-based effective number of tests (cn, lj, gao, galwey methods).

name: eigen-decomposition-numerical-implementation
description: Use when implementing a spatially aware factor-analysis/PCA model whose Gaussian-process covariance over spot coordinates would otherwise require O(n^3) operations on the dense kernel matrix, and a low-rank spectral representation is needed.

name: em-based-integrated-imputation
description: Use when omics data (Z) in a LUCID analysis contain list-wise or sporadic, missing-completely-at-random entries that make complete-case analysis infeasible, and cluster-specific omics profiles must be estimated jointly with exposures (G) and outcome (Y).

name: em-imputation-of-missing-omics-values
description: Use when an omics matrix (e.g., proteomics from the HELIX cohort) has sporadic or list-wise missing entries and you are fitting a LUCID latent-cluster model and want missing values imputed within the EM iteration.

name: embedding-coordinate-table-export
description: Use when a MuData object with RNA and ATAC modalities needs comparable 2D latent-space visualisations built from individual-modality PCs as well as joint multi-omics representations such as MOFA factors or the WNN graph, with coordinates exported per cell.

name: empirical-browns-method-implementation
description: Use when p-values or z-scores to be combined are dependent (e.g. SNPs within a gene, correlated tests) and a correlation matrix is available or must be estimated, requiring methods like kost, cn, lj, gao, galwey, ebm, yang, corstouffer or wcorstouffer.

name: emt-marker-expression-gradient-analysis
description: Use when annotated EMT single-cell data (AnnData with adata.obs['conf'] and adata.obs['var'] from DNN training dynamics) should be embedded so the graph structure signals E/M progression instead of mock vs TGF-β treatment batches.

name: enrichment-result-visualization-and-interpretation
description: Use when a differential expression step (e.g. DESeq2 on Salmon gene-level counts) has produced a DE gene list and you need GO over-representation results with dotplot/cnetplot figures and a coherence check.

name: ensembl-to-symbol-identifier-mapping
description: Use when a patient RNA-seq expression table is keyed by Ensembl gene IDs and must be reconciled with HGNC-style gene-symbol network node names before model annotation.

name: ensemble-base-learner-training-crossvalidation
description: Use when a gene-pair feature table with a binary ICB response column ('res') must be converted into an ensemble of cross-validated base-learner predictions, as a prerequisite for GA-based learner combination and riskscore computation.

name: ensemble-prediction-matrix-scoring
description: Use when base-learner prediction matrices (trainres/validatres/testres) and a GA_train-fitted model already exist and per-cohort risk scores with ROC-AUC discrimination must be computed for ICB response prediction.

name: enzyme-identifier-conversion
description: Use when an inter-layer interaction TSV carries EC numbers (e.g. 2.7.1.1 from BRENDA) but the target KEGG pathway layer indexes enzymes by KEGG reaction IDs, causing an ID namespace mismatch that must be bridged before visualization.

name: erdos-renyi-random-network-generation
description: Use when synthetic network layers are needed to benchmark or stress-test multiplex network construction scalability across a grid of layer counts (L=10–50) and node counts (N=50–5000), rather than using real multi-omic data.

name: erroneous-annotation-reannotation
description: Use when auditing annotated single-cell or spatial omics data (AnnData with a label obs key) for suspected mislabeled cells and you want training-dynamics-based reannotation plus marker-gene validation.

name: error-message-classification-into-categories
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell simulation methods and you need to capture, categorize, and quantify runtime errors per method — e.g., computing per-method error rates across 152 reference datasets in a robustness audit.

name: expectation-maximization-algorithm-implementation
description: Use when fitting a LUCID model (exposures G, omics Z, outcome Y) by maximum likelihood and a subset of observations has list-wise missing omics blocks, requiring a modified E-step/M-step that ignores Z terms for missing rows.

name: exposome-outcome-association-analysis
description: Use when analyzing mother-child cohort data (e.g., ISGlobal/ATHLETE Exposome Data Challenge, 1301 children) where an environmental exposure, an omics matrix with missing values, and a continuous outcome should be integrated to estimate latent subgroups and exposure-to-cluster-to-outcome pathways.

name: expression-outlier-filtering-iqr-mad
description: Use when raw TCGA-LUSC RNA-seq expression matrices (paired, unpaired, or cancer-only cohorts) must be quality-filtered for outliers before normalization and in silico model annotation.

name: faceted-multi-panel-visualization
description: Use when the goal is to visualize differential-expression results as faceted, thresholded volcano/scatter panels from precomputed DE tables, expression matrices + metadata, or MultiAssayExperiment objects, with per-panel significance counts.

name: false-discovery-rate-control
description: Use when single-cell count data (raw counts in a scanpy AnnData) must be screened for conditionally dependent features (e.g., gene-protein or gene-response links) while provably controlling the false discovery rate at a target level such as 0.05, 0.1, or 0.2.

name: false-discovery-rate-parameterization
description: Use when performing power or sample-size calculations for high-throughput omic data (e.g. differential feature detection across m features) where a target FDR such as alpha = 0.05 must be translated into an adjusted per-test significance level alpha.

name: fasta-indexing-and-sequence-dictionary-generation
description: Use when a GATK-compatible reference genome (e.g. GATK.GRCh38) must be made addressable for subsetting (samtools faidx / GATK Reference subsetting) or region-aware VCF tools like bcftools view -R before per-simulation reference bundles are built.

name: fastq-barcode-extraction-mismatch-tolerant
description: Use when sci-L3 combinatorial-indexing FASTQ reads must be demultiplexed into single-cell barcode identities: orienting reads on the RT primer GGGATGCAGCTCGCTCCTG and matching 8-nt Tn5 and 7-nt ligation barcodes with 1-mismatch tolerance.

name: fastq-quality-control
description: Use when paired-end FASTQ files have just been simulated or received (e.g. SimuSCoP output from the eduomics DNA branch) and quality must be assessed before variant calling or other downstream analysis.

name: fda-approved-drug-repositioning-classification
description: Use when a list of computationally predicted cancer drugs or drug combinations (e.g., from CanSeer Supplementary Data 15) must be annotated with FDA approval status and prior-literature support to separate repositioning candidates from novel hypotheses.

name: fdr-calibration-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking FDR control of a variable-selection method on count-valued (Poisson-generated) semi-synthetic responses, where OLS-based importance scores are suspected to miscalibrate but CRT-based scores should stay valid.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when testing thousands of features (e.g., 28,417 genes across 2491 tissue spots) for spatial variability or differential signal and multiplicity-controlled significance calls (BY-adjusted FDR ≤ 0.05) are needed for feature selection.

name: fdr-power-evaluation-simulation
description: Use when validating that a conditional independence testing method controls FDR at target levels and comparing its power (TPR) against linear/Gaussian baselines like OLS on semi-synthetic single-cell data.

name: fdr-tpr-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a conditional independence or feature-selection method claims FDR control and you need to quantify its empirical FDR and TPR against a ground truth (e.g. t-tests of perturbed vs unperturbed cells) and compare to OLS and marginal-test baselines.

name: fdr-tpr-operating-point-analysis
description: Use when evaluating a variable selection procedure that promises false discovery rate control: you need empirical FDR vs. TPR operating points across target FDR levels (e.g., 0.05, 0.1, 0.2) and across importance score functions of differing predictive adequacy.

name: figure-count-verification-against-reference
description: Use when a figure embeds computed annotations (e.g. per-facet up/down/neutral feature counts) and you must verify that independently recomputed statistics match what the package renders, or when reverse-engineering how cutoffs map to annotated classes.

name: fisher-method-implementation
description: Use when you have a text file of n rows x k columns of independent p-values (one variable per row, e.g. SNPs or genes across tests/traits) and need a combined per-row p-value via Fisher's method.

name: fruchterman-reingold-network-layout
description: Use when an integrated program network (e.g. program_graph.graphml built from a thresholded Pearson correlation matrix) needs a community-colored visualization to inspect modality composition of program communities.

name: gamma-distributed-brown-yang-pvalue-extension
description: Use when combining k correlated p-values (e.g. SNPs or genes in a GWAS/transcriptomics row) where Fisher's chi-square sum must be corrected for correlation, and a user-supplied correlation matrix is available.

name: gaussian-mixture-model-initialization
description: Use when fitting a LUCID model on exposures G, omics Z (possibly with sporadic or list-wise missing values), and outcome Y, and you need deterministic starting values for the EM algorithm over K latent clusters.

name: gaussian-mixture-posterior-thresholding
description: Use when continuous numeric trait columns (e.g., yogurt metabolite concentrations) must be converted to binary case/control labels for Scoary2 association testing and uncertain isolates need a principled exclusion rule.

name: gaussian-noise-injection-for-robustness-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how a multi-omics integration method degrades on intentionally corrupted inputs — e.g. comparing SSGATE vs baselines on noisy BMNC/SLN111_D1 anndata pairs under a paper's robustness protocol.

name: gdsc2-drug-sensitivity-data-retrieval
description: Use when quantitative drug-response baselines (mean IC50 per drug) are needed for GDSC2 screening against LUSC cell lines, e.g. to support CanSeer's drug repositioning and therapeutic efficacy ranking.

name: gene-alias-resolution-against-hgnc
description: Use when RNA-seq data are keyed by Ensembl gene IDs but a downstream biomolecular network model expects gene symbols, and direct symbol matches fail for some genes requiring GeneCards/HGNC alias lookup.

name: gene-annotation-trainability-scoring
description: Use when you have single-cell AnnData with per-cell confidence scores from DNN training-dynamics analysis and want to rank genes by their positive or negative association with annotation trainability (e.g., disease-related genes in mSTZ β cells).

name: gene-count-anndata-export
description: Use when the Sopa pipeline has finished aggregation (transcripts counted per cell) and you need a portable cell-by-gene matrix for scanpy/AnnData-based downstream analysis without reloading the SpatialData object.

name: gene-count-significance-dot-encoding
description: Use when you have a pathway or feature summary table with activation z-scores (fold-changes), p-values, and gene counts across conditions (e.g., brain regions and timepoints) and need a single composite heatmap visualizing all three modalities.

name: gene-expression-and-accessibility-factor-visualization
description: Use when a MuData object with paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq modalities already contains a fitted latent factor space (e.g. X_mofa in obsm) and you need to interpret what each primary factor represents biologically.

name: gene-expression-based-network-model-annotation
description: Use when a validated biomolecular regulatory network model must be personalized with normalized RNA-seq expression values before running dynamical network analyses of cell fate or treatment response.

name: gene-expression-based-signature-computation
description: Use when you have RNA-seq expression matrices from ICB-treated cohorts with a 'res' response column and need to compute/benchmark published immune signatures or compare a new score's AUC against them.

name: gene-expression-matrix-factorization
description: Use when bulk, single-cell, or spatial RNA-Seq expression matrices need unsupervised decomposition into interpretable programs, or when cohorts with mismatched features/samples must be integrated without subsetting to a shared gene set.

name: gene-expression-matrix-loading
description: Use when the input is a tab-delimited normalized count matrix (e.g. normalizedCounts_coding.tsv from GSE114007) that must be ingested in Julia before SGCRNA's CGM preprocessing and spectral clustering.

name: gene-expression-similarity-matrix-computation
description: Use when you have a normalized spatial transcriptomics expression matrix with spot coordinates and need multiple graph views (distinct similarity metrics) for multi-view graph autoencoder clustering.

name: gene-expression-variance-normalization
description: Use when ranking genes by their positive or negative association with per-cell annotation confidence (e.g. Annotatability rank_genes_conf_min_counts on mSTZ β-cell data) — variance scaling must precede correlation of expression with the confidence vector.

name: gene-filtering-for-spatial-omics-pipelines
description: Use when preprocessing spatial multi-omics data (e.g. spatial-CITE-seq with paired mRNA and protein modalities) for SMOPCA, and you must select spatially variable genes via SPARK before dimension reduction.

name: gene-identifier-mapping
description: Use when a simulation or analysis step requires harmonising gene identifiers (e.g., symbols to Entrez) before constructing GO-annotation-based similarity networks or filtering genes by annotation content.

name: gene-level-count-summarization-from-transcript-estimates
description: Use when salmon quasi-mapping quant outputs (quant.sf files) from simulated FASTQ reads must be converted to gene-level counts before running DESeq2 between simulated disease and normal groups.

name: gene-mean-variance-curve-fitting
description: Use when identifying overdispersed/highly-variable features from normalized count or intensity matrices across modalities (bulk RNA-Seq, proteomics, snRNA-Seq) where a modality-specific Poisson model does not apply.

name: gene-ontology-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have gene-to-module assignments from co-expression clustering (e.g., SGCRNA modules from Julia's SpectralClustering, or WGCNA modules such as brown4/grey) and need to test which GO terms are over-represented in each module to validate or compare module biological identity.

name: gene-ontology-overrepresentation-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a list of significant DE gene identifiers (e.g. deseq2_de_genes.txt) from simulated RNA-seq data and need GO Biological Process, Molecular Function and Cellular Component over-representation results.

name: gene-ontology-similarity-network-construction
description: Use when preparing the gene universe for RNA differential expression simulation: you need protein-coding genes on a target chromosome (e.g. chr22) that share sufficient GO-term content, with a simthreshold (default 0.3) defining edge retention.

name: gene-pair-feature-selection
description: Use when building an ICB response prediction model from RNA-seq expression/gene-pair matrices and you need batch-robust feature reduction (e.g., hundreds of gene pairs down to a top-5 support set) prior to ensemble learning.

name: gene-rank-interpretation
description: Use when a seed-gene set (e.g. jasmonate genes AT2G44810 and AT1G17420) has been run through RWR_LOE or RWR_CV on a multiplex and you must judge rank plausibility, functional enrichment, or extract/visualize the top-ranked neighborhood.

name: gene-regulation-count-annotation
description: Use when you have a precomputed DE table (log2fc, negLog10p, SampleType, timePoint) or matrix+metadata and need faceted volcano plots with per-panel up/down/neutral gene counts annotated.

name: gene-regulator-correlation-null-comparison
description: Use when validating a multi-layer GRN inference method against simulated ground truth: MOSim supplies both the count matrices (RNA-seq, miRNA-seq, TF) and the active regulatory relationships needed as reference edges and as a correlation null.

name: gene-regulatory-network-visualization
description: Use when simulated or real multi-omics count matrices plus regulator-gene associations must be inspected as multi-layered GRNs with distinct activator vs. repressor edge types.

name: gene-set-file-construction
description: Use when preparing seed, source, or target gene sets as input files for RWRtoolkit functions (RWR_LOE, RWR_ShortestPaths, RWR_CV) against a multiplex network, and genes are given as AGI identifiers.

name: genetic-algorithm-ensemble-optimization
description: Use when base-learner prediction matrices already exist (from basic_learner/basic_learner_predictor) and you must select the optimal combination of models and compute a final ensemble risk score for ICB response prediction.

name: genetic-algorithm-model-combination
description: Use when base-learner prediction matrices for training/validation/test sets already exist (from basic_learner_predictor) and an optimized ensemble scoring formula must be derived and applied to compute riskscores.

name: genie3-regression-tree-network-inference
description: Use when you have a single-cell expression dataset (scanpy AnnData with raw counts) plus a response variable, and you want to score gene-response dependencies via GENIE3 regression trees and feed those scores into calibrated conditional independence testing.

name: genome-neighborhood-visualization
description: Use when mGWAS/GWAS candidate genes need genomic-context validation — e.g. after Scoary2 flags orthogenes correlating with metabolites, to check synteny, adjacency, cluster membership, and pseudogenization across isolates.

name: genome-sequence-motif-scanning
description: Use when you need to verify or reproduce claims about restriction enzyme cut-site counts on a reference genome — e.g., comparing how frequently different single-cell Hi-C protocols (sci-L3-Hi-C's MboI vs. s3-GCC's AluI vs. droplet Hi-C's DpnII+MboII+NlaIII) fragment the genome.

name: genomic-interaction-distance-filtering
description: Use when comparing per-cell chromatin interaction counts across single-cell Hi-C protocols (sci-Hi-C, sci-L3-Hi-C, s3-GCC, droplet Hi-C) where raw valid-pair counts are inflated by linear-amplification (IVT) duplicates and short-distance interactions.

name: genomic-interval-bed-processing
description: Use when a simulation or analysis must be restricted to a specific chromosome plus exome capture regions, and reference FASTA, .dict/.fai indices, and known-variant VCFs (gnomAD, Mills, 1000G, dbSNP) need region-specific subsets.

name: genomic-interval-overlap-filtering
description: Use when a variant database such as ClinVar must be subset to exome/target capture regions on a specific chromosome and its output harmonised to the reference genome format before simulation or calling.

name: genomic-interval-pairing-and-slop-extension
description: Use when a MAPIT-seq analysis needs to convert filtered editing sites into high-confidence RBP-binding regions by requiring adjacent C-to-U and A-to-G edit clusters reproducible across replicates.

name: genus-level-feature-table-collapsing
description: Use when 16S amplicon sequencing reads (e.g. PRJNA762466 from SRA) must be denoised, classified, and collapsed to genus level with QIIME 2 before co-expression module detection with SGCRNA or WGCNA.

name: geo-expression-data-retrieval
description: Use when an analysis starts from a GEO accession (e.g., GSE68077) whose DE/expression table must be obtained and converted into log2fc / negLog10p form for MultiModalGraphics volcano plotting.

name: ggplot-object-return-validation
description: Use when wrapping MultiModalGraphics visualization calls (raw matrix, precomputed DE table, or MultiAssayExperiment input) and you need the returned S4/ggplot object for further annotation, theming, or RMarkdown embedding instead of a rendered figure.

name: ggplot-spatial-diagnostics-visualization
description: Use when you have a preprocessed Seurat spatial object (e.g., SCT-normalized HER2 or MOB assay with gene and image-feature PCA reductions) and must diagnose whether spots are more similar to spatial neighbors than non-neighbors before choosing an stImage strategy.

name: glioblastoma-molecular-subtype-annotation
description: Use when CPTAC GBM bulk RNA and protein data have been factorized into program communities (via cNMF/mosaicMPI) and patients must be labeled by classical (C1) vs mesenchymal program usage, or by cross-modality co-usage, to test survival associations such as in Figure 4E.

name: gmt-gene-set-file-preparation
description: Use when a set of literature-derived gene signatures must be formatted as a GMT file to run ssGSEA with mosaicMPI's ssgsea subcommand, e.g. to validate biological themes assigned to cNMF program communities in the CPTAC GBM landscape.

name: go-enrichment-analysis-of-de-genes
description: Use when a differential expression table (e.g., deseq2_de_genes.txt from DESeq2 on simulated RNA-seq counts) must be functionally characterized and its GO term enrichment validated for biological plausibility.

name: go-shared-term-coherence-scoring
description: Use when building tissue-specific complex priors (updated_tissue_complex_.csv) for Protrec2 and a complex record has no explicit tissue annotation, so GO-based functional coherence must stand in for a direct 1/0/0.5 relevance score.

name: gold-standard-geneset-evaluation
description: Use when you have a preassembled multiplex network and curated gene sets and need to quantify whether functionally related genes rank highly under random walk with restart, including against rewired-control baselines.

name: graph-attention-autoencoder-training
description: Use when you have two preprocessed AnnData objects (transcriptome + proteome) each carrying a pruned neighbor network in adata.uns['nbrs_net'] and need a joint low-dimensional embedding for clustering or spatially resolved downstream analysis.

name: graph-autoencoder-training
description: Use when spot/bead-level spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. 10x Visium, Slide-seq) with spatial coordinates need unsupervised spatial domain detection, 3D multi-slice reconstruction, or multimodal integration with H&E image features.

name: graph-convolutional-encoder-implementation
description: Use when spatial transcriptomics data (spot-by-gene expression matrix plus a spatial adjacency matrix for a slice) must be encoded into per-spot latent representations (Z^X, Z^A) via a graph convolutional network trained with a self-supervised DGI contrastive objective.

name: graphlet-guided-network-filtering
description: Use when integrating omic-hits (e.g., phosphoproteomic seed proteins) with a large reference interactome to infer a context-specific subnetwork, and nonspecific hub-dominated pairwise interactions must be filtered out.

name: graphlet-guided-subnetwork-inference
description: Use when you have a set of omic-hits (e.g., mutated genes or significant phosphoproteins) plus a reference interactome and need a context-specific subnetwork that trims hub-dominated, nonspecific interactions.

name: graphlet-motif-enumeration
description: Use when a seed node set of omic-hits must be expanded into a context-specific subnetwork from a large reference interactome, and nonspecific interactions/hub bias should be filtered topologically before propagation.

name: greedy-modularity-partitioning
description: Use when a program-level integration network (e.g. program_graph.graphml plus pearson.df.npz from mosaicMPI cNMF programs) must be partitioned into communities to reveal cross-modality biological themes.

name: grn-edge-recovery-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking a multi-omics GRN inference tool (e.g., MORE with the PLS1 option) against MOSim-simulated significant regulations, or when you need sensitivity/F1 of regulatory-edge recovery against a known simulated ground truth.

name: group-level-pathway-score-contrast
description: Use when per-sample iMLGAM risk scores are available for a TCGA-style pan-cancer cohort with somatic mutation and copy-number data, and the goal is group-level contrasts of pathway scores or genomic alterations between score strata.

name: gwas-snp-pvalue-reanalysis
description: Use when re-analyzing per-SNP p-values from a GWAS (SNP_p_values.txt style input) to cross-validate dependent p-value combination methods against GWAR MIN2/MAX reference results.

name: harmonic-mean-pvalue-combination
description: Use when a row of k p-values (e.g. SNPs from a GWAS) must be collapsed into one combined p-value and a robust, integration-free alternative to Fisher or Stouffer is wanted, especially when some p-values may be very small.

name: hdf5-file-hierarchy-verification
description: Use when a MuData object has been written to .h5mu and you must confirm the HDF5 layout exposes per-modality AnnData storage, or when reading a single modality back (e.g. via mu.read('file.h5mu/rna')) to validate interoperable serialisation.

name: hdf5-multimodal-data-serialisation
description: Use when a multi-modality MuData object (e.g. paired 'rna'/'atac' or 'rna'/'prot' PBMC assays) must be saved to or loaded from an .h5mu file, especially when analysis spans Python, R, or Julia.

name: hdwgcna-module-identification
description: Use when benchmarking co-expression module detection on normalised single-cell or spatial transcriptomic data (e.g. Seurat-processed Visium kidney GSE261545) and the hdWGCNA arm of an SGCRNA-vs-hdWGCNA comparison is needed.

name: he-image-feature-extraction
description: Use when a 10x Visium (or similar SRT) dataset ships an H&E histology image aligned to spot coordinates, and spatial-domain clustering should exploit morphological information to lift clustering accuracy (e.g. MCGAE ARI 0.53→0.64).

name: he-image-patch-embedding-computation
description: Use when a SpatialData object contains both segmented cells with transcript counts and an aligned H&E image, and the goal is to derive morphological niches from H&E rather than expression alone.

name: held-out-prediction-error-evaluation
description: Use when running VI-VS/CRT variable selection and you must choose an importance score function (e.g., xy_linear OLS vs. MLP with n_hidden capacity), or when comparing FDR-TPR trade-offs across importance score choices in semi-synthetic experiments.

name: her2-breast-cancer-marker-biology
description: Use when HER2 H1 stImage objects with WNN multimodal integration clusters (clusterNum = 6) must be biologically validated against pathologist-annotated regions via spatial marker gene plots.

name: hi-c-compartment-eigenvector-decomposition
description: Use when single-cell or bulk Hi-C contact maps (cool files) must be decomposed into A/B compartment eigenvectors and quantitatively compared across conditions via eigenvector correlation.

name: hi-c-cutter-frequency-comparison
description: Use when comparing restriction enzyme cutting frequencies across single-cell Hi-C protocols, or when reproducing the reported MboI (~7M), AluI (13M), and combination-digest (~30M) cut-site totals on the hs37d5/GRCh37 reference to explain differences in cis-interaction capture.

name: hic-valid-pair-parsing
description: Use when comparing per-cell informative chromatin interaction counts across single-cell Hi-C protocols from valid-pairs (e.g. GSM2254217) or pairix contact files, where duplicate IVT amplification products must be removed by collapsing to unique restriction fragment pairs.

name: hierarchical-accuracy-score-aggregation
description: Use when raw metric x property scores from the 49-method benchmark exist and a single comparable accuracy score per simulation method (SRT and scRNA-seq simulators) must be produced.

name: hierarchical-gene-clustering-on-correlation-matrix
description: Use when running VI-VS/VIVS multi-resolution hypothesis testing on single-cell count data and you need gene groups (clusters) as testable features in addition to individual genes.

name: highly-variable-feature-selection
description: Use when preparing normalized count matrices (e.g. bulk RNA-Seq STAR counts, CPTAC proteomics, snRNA-Seq feature counts) for factorization and you need a modality-agnostic overdispersed feature subset instead of cNMF's scRNA-Seq-calibrated Poisson model.

name: highly-variable-gene-selection-cite-seq
description: Use when single-cell multi-omics data (e.g. CITE-seq PBMC or SMAGE-seq PBMC3K/PBMC10K) lacks spatial coordinates and you need pseudo-spatial locations for a spatially aware model like SMOPCA.

name: histogram-distribution-visualization
description: Use when a validation step requires inspecting the empirical distribution of a per-pair metric (e.g., IOMA segmentation-conflict scores) against a published pattern or threshold range.

name: histological-image-tile-segmentation
description: Use when a spatial transcriptomics workflow has a paired H&E image and spot coordinate table and needs per-spot morphological image embeddings to fuse with expression and spatial-position views.

name: histology-image-feature-extraction
description: Use when raw H&E images paired with ST spot coordinates or Visium (filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 + spatial folder) must be turned into per-spot VGG16 image-feature and RGB quantile matrices as the image modality of an stImage object.

name: homer-de-novo-motif-discovery
description: Use when you have a BED file of high-confidence RBP edit clusters (e.g., from the MAPIT-seq hc_cluster step) and need to de novo discover and validate the RBP's known binding motif against a permuted control background.

name: hvfeature-selection-overdispersion
description: Use when preparing a bulk or single-cell RNA-Seq expression matrix (e.g. an AnnData h5ad) for cNMF factorization or downstream integration in mosaicMPI, and over-dispersed genes must be identified to restrict factorization to informative features.

name: hybrid-minp-cct-pvalue-combination
description: Use when p-values to be combined are dependent (correlated) — e.g. SNP/gene rows from a GWAS or transcriptomics study — and a robust, correlation-free combined p-value is needed without numerical integration.

name: hydra-configuration-file-generation
description: Use when running SPArrOW pipeline steps (e.g. im.segment on a resolve_example spatial object) and you need to locate and archive the Hydra-generated .yaml config that encodes that step's parameters.

name: hypergeometric-enrichment-testing
description: Use when louvain modules from pyPARAGON-inferred subnetworks (e.g., 105 CPTAC breast cancer tumor networks) must be annotated with GO biological processes or KEGG pathways via a hypergeometric test to support patient stratification.

name: hyperparameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when a fixed hyperparameter of a multi-omics integrator (e.g., SSGATE's balance parameter weighting self-reconstruction vs. triplet loss) must be swept while others stay constant, to validate defaults via clustering metrics.

name: ic50-outlier-removal
description: Use when computing robust per-drug average IC50 values from GDSC2 (or similar) drug sensitivity datasets for a specific cancer subtype's cell lines, and raw IC50 replicates contain outliers that would skew group means.

name: ic50-pharmacological-data-integration
description: Use when you must rank candidate drugs for a personalized cancer model by converting drug IC50 sensitivity data plus patient-specific normalized expression into NDAS values.

name: icb-response-label-matching
description: Use when scoring ICB responder vs non-responder cohorts with a fitted iMLGAM ga_fit model: prediction matrices (trainres, validatres, testres) lack the outcome column and must be re-aligned to 'res' labels by row-name intersection before predict() and ROC-AUC evaluation.

name: icb-response-risk-score-prediction
description: Use when RNA-seq cohorts from ICB/immunotherapy-treated patients (with a 'res' response outcome column) need a predictive risk score and it must be compared head-to-head with published immune signatures such as TIDE, IFNγ, CYT, or IPS.

name: igraph-toy-network-generation
description: Use when you need a small, fully controlled multiplex network to isolate parameter effects (e.g., tau per-layer seed weighting) in RWR, or to reproduce regression tests against an updated RWRtoolkit implementation.

name: ilp-causal-network-optimization
description: Use when multi-omics case-vs-control data (transcriptomics, proteomics, phosphoproteomics) yield inferred protein activities plus a user-defined set of perturbed molecules/receptors (e.g. EGF, MTOR/AMPK, Flt3) that must be connected through a prior knowledge causal network.

name: image-augmentation-pipelines
description: Use when you have Visium H&E slides with a spot coordinate table and need per-spot morphological image embeddings (e.g. Z-morph) to integrate with spatial gene expression.

name: image-feature-profile-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking multi-modal ST integration strategies requires synthetic paired expression + image-feature data with controlled cluster counts and dropout rates and trusted ground-truth labels.

name: imlgam-risk-score-computation
description: Use when a GA-trained iMLGAM model (ga_fit) exists and per-patient ICB response risk scores must be computed from training (70%), validation (30%), and test prediction matrices, then evaluated for discrimination (ROC-AUC) against the 'res' outcome labels.

name: immune-cell-infiltration-estimation
description: Use when a cohort has computed iMLGAM risk scores (with 'riskscore' and 'res' columns per sample) and the goal is to contrast tumor microenvironment immune metrics — leukocyte, lymphocyte, TIL, CD8+ T cell, fibroblast, Danaher scores — between low- and high-score groups.

name: immune-signature-scoring
description: Use when ICB/immunotherapy cohort RNA-seq data with a binary 'res' response column are available and you must score patients with the iMLGAM riskscore and/or published immune signatures (TIDE, CYT, IFNγ, TLS, IPS, expIS, etc.) and compare their predictive AUC.

name: immunotherapy-cohort-response-annotation
description: Use when cohort-level RNA-seq/ICI datasets with a binary immunotherapy response column ('res'), PD-L1 expression, and TMB are available and the goal is to test whether the iMLGAM score outperforms existing biomarkers.

name: immunotherapy-response-risk-scoring
description: Use when building a predictive risk score for immunotherapy (ICB) response from RNA-seq gene-pair features, needing ensemble ML with automated base-learner optimization via a genetic algorithm.

name: implementation-behavior-regression-comparison
description: Use when an algorithm library has been updated/forked (e.g., RWRtoolkit vs original RandomWalkRestartMH) and you must confirm that a parameter now behaves as documented rather than being silently ignored.

name: importance-score-model-fitting
description: Use when decision support for choosing the importance score T(X,Y,S) in VI-VS: when testing conditional gene dependencies and deciding between a linear score (xy_linear=True) or nonlinear MLP scores, or when held-out predictive performance should be used to justify the score choice.

name: imputation-method-benchmarking
description: Use when choosing among imputation strategies for omics data with sporadic missingness (missing completely at random in individual entries), or when complete-case analysis is infeasible and bias of downstream clustering estimates must be quantified.

description: Use when a validated biomolecular regulatory network model (e.g.

name: in-silico-restriction-digestion
description: Use when you need to reproduce or compare in-silico cut-site counts for restriction enzymes on a reference genome, e.g. to justify enzyme choice for a Hi-C protocol or quantify 'how many fewer sites' one cutter has than another.

name: integer-linear-programming-formulation
description: Use when an experiment design problem must be solved by cost-minimization over discrete per-omic sample sizes subject to per-omic power (omicPower), average power (averagePower), FDR, max.size, and optional equalSize constraints in a multi-omics power study.

name: integrated-program-community-interpretation
description: Use when a community-by-sample usage matrix from mosaicMPI integration exists and you need to associate communities with categorical metadata (e.g. EGFR/NF1/PDGFRA/BRAF alterations, subtypes, cell types) or numerical metadata (e.g. tumor purity).

name: inter-batch-adjacency-distance-computation
description: Use when jointly analyzing consecutive spatial transcriptomics sections (e.g., seven Slide-seq hippocampal slices) where per-section bead coordinates must be linked by cross-batch adjacency edges before 3D spatial domain clustering.

name: inter-layer-edge-construction-in-2-5d-networks
description: Use when a trans-omic interaction table (source/target layer index, node-table column, attribute value, interaction type) must be realized as edges connecting stacked omic layers in an existing Cytoscape 2.5D network.

name: inter-layer-edge-integration
description: Use when you have a layered KEGG-based pathway visualization (e.g., rno04910 over rno01100 layers, or the five-layer mouse liver glucose-response network) and tabular trans-omic connectivity data that must be joined across layers by KEGG-compatible molecule IDs.

name: inter-layer-transition-parameter-configuration
description: Use when building a multiplex network from multiple layer edge-list files and you must set the inter-layer transition probability (delta) and layer codes before running RWR.

name: interactome-dataset-integration
description: Use when a task requires feeding a large prior-knowledge reference interactome plus a seed set of omic-hits into a network-propagation pipeline to infer a context-specific signaling subnetwork.

name: interactome-edge-confidence-weighting
description: Use when you have a reference interactome with edge confidence scores, a weighted omic-hits seed set, and a GGN, and you need to rank edges to reconstruct a context-specific subnetwork.

name: iterative-sample-size-convergence-testing
description: Use when estimating the optimal sample size for an ML classification task on multi-omic data, and you need to determine how many sampling ticks suffice before fitting a learning-curve model to tick-vs-ER data.

name: jaccard-index-threshold-filtering
description: Use when preparing RNA-seq simulation inputs and you must restrict candidate genes to a biologically coherent, GO-annotated set (e.g. protein-coding genes on a single chromosome such as chr22) before count-matrix generation.

name: julia-rcall-interop-bioinformatics
description: Use when a Julia co-expression pipeline (SGCRNA) has produced gene module assignments and you need R functionality — e.g. GO enrichment, WGCNA module comparison — executed inside the same Julia session via RCall.

name: julia-sgcrna-pipeline-execution
description: Use when analyzing a gene/multi-omic expression matrix (e.g. RNA normalized counts in TSV) to identify co-expression modules without assuming scale-free topology or hand-tuning WGCNA's soft-thresholding parameters.

name: k-means-clustering-of-temporal-expression-profiles
description: Use when you need to validate that simulated multi-omics count data (e.g. MOSim bulk RNA-seq with time-series design, biological replicates and DEGs) reproduce the temporal expression profiles specified in the simulation settings.

name: kaplan-meier-survival-analysis
description: Use when single-modality (RNA-only or protein-only) program-usage stratification of CPTAC GBM patients shows no survival differences and a combined-modality classical+mesenchymal co-usage stratification is needed.

name: kaplan-meier-survival-curve-estimation
description: Use when patient samples have been partitioned into groups (e.g., network-based clusters) and merged with clinical metadata (survival time, censoring status), and you must test whether one group shows significantly worse survival (p < 0.05).

name: kde-based-distribution-comparison
description: Use when scoring the accuracy of scRNA-seq or SRT simulation methods: the data property under evaluation is 2-D (e.g., cell–cell correlation, CCC) and you need the KDE-based distance between real and simulated distributions.

name: kegg-database-querying
description: Use when an interaction table or node list uses identifiers from a source database (e.g. BRENDA EC numbers like 2.7.1.1) that must be converted to KEGG reaction IDs (rn:RXXXXX) or KEGG gene IDs before integrating with KEGG pathway maps.

name: kegg-pathway-kgml-retrieval
description: Use when building a stacked 2.5D trans-omic network in Cytoscape whose layers are KEGG pathways (e.g. insulin signaling rno04910/mmu04910 over metabolic maps rno01100/mmu01100), requiring KGML retrieval and ID conversion to KEGG-compatible IDs.

name: kegg-pathway-overrepresentation-analysis
description: Use when patient- or condition-specific inferred networks must be partitioned into functional modules and tested for KEGG pathway over-representation to reproduce cluster-level pathway frequency analyses (e.g., Fig. 4D Ras-module style extraction).

name: kendall-correlation-regulatory-interaction-validation
description: Use when validating single-cell multi-omics simulations where a ground-truth set of gene-peak regulatory interactions must be shown to exhibit correlations stronger than random non-regulatory feature pairs.

name: kinase-substrate-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have phosphoproteomic data (UniProt ID, gene_name, aminoacid, position, sequence window, difference, logpval) from a perturbation experiment and need kinase/phosphatase activity estimates as input to network reconstruction.

name: kinase-substrate-percentile-threshold-filtering
description: Use when building a prior knowledge network for SignalingProfiler 2.0 that must include kinase–substrate edges from the Ser/Thr Kinome Atlas, and you need to decide which atlas relations are stringent enough for PKN edges versus regulon-level inclusion.

name: kmeans-binary-clustering
description: Use when a phenotypic/omics trait table contains continuous numeric measurements (e.g. yogurt metabolome traits) that Scoary2 requires as binary (0/1) presence/absence labels before mGWAS association.

name: kmeans-clustering-of-spatial-transcriptomics-cells
description: Use when you have an allocated, preprocessed cell-by-gene AnnData table from a spatial transcriptomics pipeline (e.g. SPArrOW tb.allocate followed by tb.preprocess_transcriptomics) and need unsupervised cell clustering.

name: kmeans-module-assignment
description: Use when a co-expression analysis needs module (cluster) assignment for genes after spectral embedding, specifically within the SGCRNA pipeline where CGM has produced CorData and GradData matrices and spectral clustering must yield per-gene cluster labels.

name: knn-neighborhood-graph-construction
description: Use when preparing single-cell or spatially resolved multi-omics AnnData objects for SSGATE training and you must build cell-cell neighborhood graphs from expression profiles ('X_pca') or spatial coordinates ('spatial').

name: kost-polynomial-correlation-adjustment
description: Use when combining k dependent p-values (or z-scores) per row of an n x k input file where a correlation matrix for the tests is available or can be estimated, and a correlation-aware alternative to Fisher's or Bonferroni's method is needed.

name: ks-goodness-of-fit-testing
description: Use when judging simulator accuracy: you have a real reference expression matrix plus simulated matrices and need distribution-level distances between properties such as library size (LS), per-cell zero counts (FZC), or cell–cell correlation (CCC).

name: label-to-polygon-vectorization
description: Use when you hold a segmentation labels layer from a spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g. RESOLVE mouse liver) and need polygon shapes as the geometric input for transcript allocation.

name: label-transfer-between-datasets
description: Use when an unannotated cohort (e.g. Mayo-PDX GBM bulk RNA-Seq, n=66) must receive subtype or metadata labels from an annotated reference cohort (e.g. CPTAC) after mosaicMPI program-network integration, without shared sample IDs or full feature overlap.

name: latent-cluster-model-selection-bic
description: Use when fitting a LUCID model with lucid()/estimate_lucid() and the number of latent subgroups K is unknown and must be data-driven rather than fixed a priori.

name: latent-representation-pseudo-r2-evaluation
description: Use when comparing latent embeddings from competing multi-omics dimension reduction methods on the same spots/cells and you need clustering agreement (AMI/NMI/ARI) plus latent quality (McFadden pseudo R2) in one table.

name: layer-edge-list-aggregation-across-omics-networks
description: Use when you have ≥2 edge-list files describing different relationship types between a shared node set and need a combined multiplex network object for random-walk analysis or layer-similarity statistics.

name: layer-pairwise-jaccard-similarity-computation
description: Use when you have a preassembled multiplex network object (e.g., the 9-layer Arabidopsis thaliana multiplex with delta = 0.5) and need per-layer node/edge counts plus edge-wise overlap between every pair of layers.

name: lazy-image-bounding-box-extraction
description: Use when computing per-cell staining-intensity aggregates on large multi-channel images with polygon cell boundaries, where loading full raster masks would exhaust memory.

name: lc-ms-gc-ms-data-preprocessing
description: Use when raw LC-MS or GC-MS metabolite abundance matrices (metabolites x isolates, e.g. yogurt fermentations with 182 added starter strains) need normalization and feature filtering before dimensionality reduction or association testing.

name: leiden-clustering-metric-evaluation
description: Use when you have SSGATE (or comparable) integrated embeddings from paired transcriptome/proteome single-cell data (e.g. BMNC, SLN111_D1) and need to quantitatively compare integration quality across hyperparameter settings via label-annotated clustering.

name: leiden-clustering-of-integrated-embeddings
description: Use when you have a learned joint multi-omics embedding (e.g. SSGATE out_dims=30 output for transcriptomics-proteomics data in AnnData/h5ad) and need discrete cell clusters that can be checked for spatial aggregation against tissue anatomy.

name: leiden-clustering-resolution-sweep
description: Use when you have an integrated embedding from a multi-omics method (SSGATE, MOFA+, Seurat v5, totalVI, scMM) on .h5ad data and need multiple Leiden clusterings at resolutions 0.1–1.0 to compute Purity, HS, ARI, and NMI against ground-truth labels.

name: leiden-graph-clustering-of-cell-by-gene-matrix
description: Use when a preprocessed cell-by-gene AnnData table (output of tb.preprocess_transcriptomics) needs unsupervised cluster assignments per cell in a SPArrOW spatial transcriptomics workflow.

name: limma-voom-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when normalized RNA-seq count matrices (e.g. TMM-normalized after NOISeq filtering, from bulk RNA-seq simulation or real data) need differential expression calls to feed downstream GRN inference or benchmarking.

name: list-wise-missing-omics-imputation
description: Use when an exposure/omics/outcome (G, Z, Y) matrix intended for LUCID integrative clustering has list-wise missing rows in the omics block (e.g., only a subset of the 1301 HELIX/Exposome Data Challenge children have measured proteomics) and you need unbiased cluster estimates.

name: list-wise-missingness-handling
description: Use when a multi-omics dataset shows list-wise missingness — entire omics (Z) rows missing for a subset of individuals — and LUCID integrated clustering of G, Z, and Y must still be fit.

name: literature-corroboration-curation
description: Use when a computational method (e.g. CanSeer drug scores) has produced predicted mono-targeted drugs or drug combinations that must be triaged into FDA-approved, literature-corroborated, repositioned, or novel categories.

name: log-cpm-feature-engineering
description: Use when raw gene expression counts in a scanpy AnnData object must be converted to predictor features (e.g., squared log-CPM) for VI-VS variable selection or conditional randomization testing.

name: log-rank-hazard-comparison
description: Use when per-patient program usage (e.g. CLA/MES communities) is available in both RNA and protein modalities, clinical survival metadata exists, and single-modality stratifications fail to separate hazards.

name: log-rank-survival-difference-testing
description: Use when patient samples have both cluster assignments from network-based stratification (e.g., pyPARAGON clusters of 105 breast cancer tumors) and clinical metadata with survival time and censoring status, and the goal is to test whether clusters differ in overall survival.

name: log10-pvalue-transformation
description: Use when comparing combined p-values produced by different p-value combination methods (e.g., metacp vs GWAR on the 67 type-2 diabetes GWAS SNPs) and you need an R2 agreement measure on a comparable scale.

name: logit-space-equal-weight-evidence-averaging
description: Use when recovering missing proteins in MS proteomics by combining multiple probabilistic evidence sources (prior, co-complex support, complex confidence) and you need a stable averaging rule that resists domination by extreme values.

name: louvain-community-clustering-single-cell
description: Use when single-cell AnnData carries per-cell training-dynamics scores ('conf', 'var') from Annotatability and the goal is to cluster cells by annotation-trainability signal, e.g. recovering disease/intermediate/healthy-like β cell states and comparing treatment subgroups.

name: lower-is-better-metric-inversion
description: Use when combining evaluation metrics for scRNA-seq/SRT simulation benchmarking where some metrics (e.g., distance/error metrics) improve as values decrease, and scores must be oriented so higher normalized values always mean better performance before aggregation.

name: lucid-integrative-clustering-model-fitting
description: Use when jointly clustering individuals on exposures (G), omics (Z), and an outcome (Y) — e.g. prenatal hexachlorobenzene (HCB) + proteomics + childhood BMI z-score — especially when the omics block contains list-wise or sporadic missing values.

name: lucid-model-em-extension
description: Use when fitting a LUCID model to exposures (G), omics (Z), and outcome (Y) data where a subset of observations has list-wise missing omics blocks, and you need the EM algorithm modified via the likelihood partition of Eqs. 12-13.

name: lung-tissue-specific-complex-annotation
description: Use when a proteomics recovery task needs tissue-aware complex priors — e.g., running Protrec2 with --tissue lung on an expression matrix and requiring per-complex confidence values across 27 tissue types.

name: machine-learning-base-learner-training
description: Use when building the iMLGAM ensemble: training cohorts with an outcome column 'res' and gene-pair feature columns need multiple base-learner models whose per-model predictions feed GA-based stacking.

name: machine-learning-classification-error-control
description: Use when designing a multi-omic classification study and you need the predicted sample size (PSS) a learner such as random forest requires to hit a target classification error rate (e.g., 0.01) on pilot omic feature matrices.

name: machine-learning-sample-size-estimation
description: Use when designing a multi-omic ML classification study and you need the number of samples required to control classification ER, given pilot multi-omic data with per-tick average classification error rates.

name: macrophage-subset-spatial-interaction-analysis
description: Use when a task requires quantifying cell-type/cell-type and cell-type/niche spatial interaction via hop distances on a SpatialData object, e.g. verifying niche-specific macrophage co-localization in MERSCOPE liver data.

name: mapit-score-matrix-clustering
description: Use when you have a single-cell MAPIT-score matrix (e.g., Supplementary Table 28, 1,499 cells × genes) plus co-profiled transcriptome and need to find cell subpopulations with distinct RBP-binding preferences or correlate binding strength with target RNA abundance across cell-cycle phases.

name: mapit-seq-edit-statistics-interpretation
description: Use when a MAPIT-seq run has produced a differential editing statistics table and you need to threshold it into a target list, or when reproducing MAPIT ∩ PAR-CLIP overlap counts (e.g., 4,769 G3BP1 targets in HEK293T cells).

name: mapit-seq-enzyme-configuration-comparison
description: Use when MAPIT-seq editing calls exist for both dual-editor and single-deaminase (hADAR2dd-only or rAPOBEC1-only) samples and you need to measure which enzyme configuration recovers more known RBP targets.

name: mapit-seq-pipeline-execution
description: Use when paired-end FASTQ data from MAPIT-seq experiments needs alignment, abundant-RNA filtering, RNA editing event calling (A-to-G and C-to-U), or differential editing-based RBP target calling.

name: mapman-annotation-gene-set-curation
description: Use when you need a curated, functionally coherent seed gene set (e.g. genes sharing a MAPMAN 'Jasmonate' term) to validate a multiplex network with RWR_CV, and you must write it as a two-column set/gene file with matched negative/loosely-connected control genes.

name: marginal-likelihood-hyperparameter-optimization
description: Use when fitting a SMOPCA-style Gaussian spatial latent-factor model to multi-omics matrices with spot coordinates, and the Matérn kernel lengthscale gamma must be learned by maximizing the closed-form marginal likelihood rather than set by hand.

name: marker-based-cluster-annotation-verification
description: Use when clustering labels (K-means, Specter, Seurat, etc.) have been assigned to spots/cells and the biological identity of each cluster must be validated against known marker genes or proteins.

name: marker-gene-alignment-validation
description: Use when cells have been reannotated by Annotatability's reannotation module and you must confirm the new labels biologically by checking whether canonical marker expression (e.g., Gad1 for inhibitory neurons) now matches the reassigned cell type.

name: marker-gene-trainability-ranking
description: Use when an AnnData object already carries per-cell confidence ('conf') and variability ('var') scores from DNN training dynamics and you need to rank genes by positive or negative association with annotation trainability, e.g. to verify erroneous annotations via marker gene expression.

name: matern-kernel-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when you need to test whether a spatially aware dimension reduction and clustering pipeline (e.g., SMOPCA on simulated spatial multi-omics data) is robust to kernel parameters, normalization methods, and gene-selection strategies.

name: max-expression-0-1-normalization
description: Use when preprocessing raw TCGA-LUSC RNA-seq matrices for CanSeer: you have merged normal (N) and cancer (Cs) sample sets per use case and need 0-1 scaled expressions that feed patient-specific drug score (DS) computation.

name: mean-ic50-computation-per-drug
