description: Use when reproducing CanSeer's GDSC2 drug-sensitivity screening: you have per-cell-line, per-drug IC50 measurements, an LUSC cell-line annotation, and a list of candidate drugs, and need outlier-filtered mean IC50 per drug.

name: mean-rank-gene-meta-analysis
description: Use when several independent CRISPR/Cas9 screening cohorts must be aggregated into one consensus gene ranking to prioritize immune-evasion or ICB-response targets.

name: median-auc-method-comparison
description: Use when evaluating how clustering/prediction performance of methods for handling list-wise missing omics data degrades as missingness ratio increases, to select the most stable imputation-integrated clustering approach.

name: memory-footprint-benchmarking
description: Use when you must quantify or validate the memory savings of Sopa's chunk-wise polygon-based channel averaging over full raster-mask loading, e.g. when adopting the aggregation step for large multi-channel images with millions of cells.

name: memory-runtime-benchmark-profiling
description: Use when evaluating whether segmentation of large image-based spatial omics data (e.g. Xenium, MERSCOPE) is memory/time-limited, or when validating that Sopa's patch-based strategy reduces peak RAM and runtime versus whole-image baselines.

name: merfish-spatial-omics-analysis
description: Use when analyzing annotated MERFISH spatial transcriptomics AnnData (e.g. mouse hypothalamic preoptic region with a 'label' obs column) to detect or fix erroneous cell-type annotations via DNN training dynamics.

name: meta-analysis-of-duplicate-rows
description: Use when the metacp input text file (n rows x k columns of p-values or z-scores) contains multiple rows for the same SNP/gene/probe and per-variable combined p-values should be computed after a prior meta-analysis of the duplicate rows.

name: meta-analysis-software-evaluation
description: Use when choosing or benchmarking software for combining independent or dependent p-values and you need to verify which combination methods each candidate package (e.g. metacp, poolr, metap) actually implements.

name: metabolite-annotation-table-extraction
description: Use when a paper's supplementary table reports metabolite identity confirmations by analytical standards (measured m/z, CAS number, mass error in ppm, retention-time error) and these annotations must be extracted, validated, and exported.

name: metabolite-protein-interaction-data-processing
description: Use when a trans-omic interaction table (e.g. BRENDA allosteric metabolite-protein TSV) carries EC numbers in one column but the target pathway layer (KEGG rn map) requires reaction IDs, blocking cross-layer edge attachment.

name: metabolite-trait-gwas-correction
description: Use when running mGWAS of a pan-genome orthogene matrix against a large numeric phenotypic dataset (e.g. metabolomics traits per strain) and you must control false positives with trait-aware correction before nominating candidate genes.

name: metabolomics-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when you have a metabolite-by-isolate abundance matrix (hundreds to thousands of features) and need to test whether samples cluster by a known categorical label, such as starter-culture taxonomy.

name: metagenomic-amplicon-denoising-and-taxonomy-assignment
description: Use when raw 16S amplicon reads (e.g. from an SRA accession like PRJNA762466) must be denoised, feature-classified, and collapsed to genus level into a count matrix that will feed co-expression network methods such as SGCRNA or WGCNA.

name: methylation-effect-size-filtering
description: Use when a MultiPower run on a multi-omic design with Methyl-seq (or another high-feature-count omic) yields an inflated optimal sample size driven by low-effect methylation features, and you want to test whether filtering boosts power.

name: microbial-gwas-association-testing
description: Use when a pan-genome gene presence/absence matrix (orthogroups from OrthoFinder or Roary) and a numeric phenotype table (e.g. 3889 metabolomics traits for 182 yogurt isolates) are available and the goal is to associate orthogenes with traits.

name: microbial-phenotype-data-preprocessing
description: Use when a phenotypic trait table contains continuous (numeric) columns that must be binarized before Scoary2 genome-wide association, and uncertain isolates (posterior probability < 0.85) should be excluded rather than forced into a binary label.

name: min-max-scaling-per-data-property
description: Use when raw metric scores from simulated vs. real scRNA-seq/SRT comparisons sit on incommensurate scales (e.g., distance/error metrics vs. correlation-like metrics) and must be brought onto a common [0,1] scale before aggregating into a per-method accuracy score.

name: mirrored-negative-correlation-null-estimation
description: Use when constructing an anchor edge list from pairwise program correlation matrices across CPTAC-style datasets where feature overlap is incomplete and a dataset-pair-specific correlation cutoff is needed.

name: mislabeled-cell-detection-auroc
description: Use when auditing cell-type annotations of single-cell or spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. MERFISH .h5ad with a 'label' obs column) and you need to quantify, via AUROC, how well confidence/variability training-dynamics scores detect synthetically mislabeled cells versus classifier-based baselines.

name: missing-data-likelihood-derivation
description: Use when fitting a LUCID integrative clustering model (G exposures, Z omics, Y outcome) where a subset of observations has list-wise missing omics data, and you need to modify EM responsibilities and M-step updates for the missing block.

name: mlp-training
description: Use when H&E-derived spot tile features must be converted into a low-dimensional spot-level embedding that can be fused with gene expression and spatial position views in a multimodal spatial transcriptomics model.

name: modality-attention-weight-normalization
description: Use when chained modality-specific spatial representations (expression, spatial adjacency, morphological image features) share the same n_spots dimension and must be fused into a single unified embedding with per-spot attention weights.

name: modality-concordance-diagnostics
description: Use when preparing a spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g. HER2 ST or Visium) for spatial-aware or multi-modal analysis and you must decide whether spots are more similar to spatial neighbors than non-neighbors before choosing an integration strategy.

name: model-output-reference-validation
description: Use when a literature-derived signaling network (e.g., the updated Cho et al. human signaling network) must be re-analyzed to reproduce originally published cell fate propensities before applying patient-specific annotations or drug perturbations.

name: model-robustness-threshold-evaluation
description: Use when a literature-derived biomolecular network model must be validated as robust to small input perturbations before personalization, by measuring SEM of cell fate propensities (e.g. normal proliferation, apoptosis) across bootstrap states.

name: module-spatial-enrichment-mapping
description: Use when gene co-expression modules have already been clustered (SGCRNA SpectralClustering or hdWGCNA) and you need to attribute each module to tissue regions or traits, e.g. spatial spots in a Visium dataset.

name: molecule-id-mapping-to-kegg-ids
description: Use when input connectivity tables or pathway layers contain non-KEGG molecule identifiers (e.g., Ensembl, gene symbols) that must be harmonized to KEGG gene IDs and EC numbers before building a multi-layered trans-omic network.

name: monocle3-pseudotime-inference
description: Use when an SSGATE (or similar) multi-omics integration result in AnnData form, with cluster labels and an integrated embedding, must be validated by ordering cells along pseudo-time and comparing against a PAGA trajectory graph.

name: monte-carlo-simulation-design
description: Use when you must quantify how a latent-clustering or integrative-omics method degrades as list-wise missingness increases, by simulating data with known truth and benchmarking imputation competitors.

name: mudata-container-management
description: Use when a task involves paired multi-omics single-cell data (e.g. 10x Multiome filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 with 'rna' and 'atac' modalities) that must be loaded, filtered, aligned across modalities, or saved as a single container for joint analysis.

name: multi-assay-experiment-data-handling
description: Use when the input is a MultiAssayExperiment (MAE) object and the goal is a thresholded, faceted volcano scatterplot with per-panel upregulated/downregulated/neutral feature counts rather than plotting a precomputed DE table or raw matrix.

name: multi-classifier-benchmarking
description: Use when a new cell-annotation-error score must be quantitatively compared to established per-cell mislabel-detection baselines on semi-synthetically perturbed annotated single-cell or spatial data, using AUROC vs mislabeled fraction.

name: multi-database-complex-integration
description: Use when a complex-based recovery or enrichment method needs a broader complex prior than CORUM alone (only 694 human complexes of size >=5), and CORUM, STRING, Complex Portal, and Reactome sources are available to merge and deduplicate.

name: multi-database-sign-format-compliance
description: Use when you need to build or refresh a SignalingProfiler-compliant PKN from public causal-interaction resources (SIGNOR, PsP, OmniPath, Ser/Thr Kinome Atlas) for human or mouse contexts.

name: multi-layer-2-5d-network-stacking
description: Use when multi-omics connectivity tables must be visualized as stacked pathway layers in 3D (2.5D) space with regulatory edges between omic layers, e.g., reproducing Yugi/Kokaji-style trans-omic network figures.

name: multi-layer-grn-inference
description: Use when you have matched bulk RNA-seq counts plus at least one regulatory omics layer (miRNA-seq, TF, ATAC/ChIP-seq) and need to infer cross-omics regulator-gene interactions, ideally with a simulated ground truth for validation.

name: multi-layer-metadata-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a community-by-sample usage matrix from a mosaicMPI landscape integration plus a sample metadata table, and need to link communities to driver genotypes, subtypes, cell types, or purity.

name: multi-layer-node-matching-by-node-table-attributes
description: Use when a 7-column trans-omic interaction table (source/target layer index, node-table column, attribute value, interaction type) must be connected onto an already-stacked multi-layer Cytoscape network.

name: multi-metric-data-property-comparison
description: Use when you have paired simulated and real reference single-cell RNA-seq or spatially resolved transcriptomics datasets and need to quantify how faithfully the simulation reproduces real data properties.

name: multi-modal-integration-analysis
description: Use when spatial transcriptomics data contain both histology image features and gene expression, and the goal is joint clustering of spots across modalities, e.g. comparing WNN vs MCIA vs tICA vs Spectrum against annotated tissue regions.

name: multi-omics-annotated-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when you have fold-change and p-value/q-value matrices (plus metadata such as CNA/mutation status) from multi-omics data and need a single annotated heatmap with overlaid significance stars and integrated legends.

name: multi-omics-count-matrix-processing
description: Use when raw count matrices from different -omics modalities (bulk RNA, mass spectrometry proteomics, snRNA-Seq) must be converted to mosaicMPI's h5ad inputs and checked for missing, negative, or zero-variance features before overdispersion modeling.

name: multi-omics-dimension-reduction
description: Use when you have paired multi-omics count matrices (e.g. gene expression + protein ADT, or ATAC gene activity + mRNA) measured on the same cells/spots and need an integrated low-dimensional representation for clustering, with or without spatial coordinates.

name: multi-omics-embedding-fusion
description: Use when you have paired transcriptomic and proteomic single-cell or spatial multi-omics data in AnnData format with precomputed neighborhood graphs (adata.uns['nbrs_net']) and need a fused low-dimensional joint embedding per cell for downstream analysis.

name: multi-omics-integrative-clustering
description: Use when you have an exposure matrix, an incomplete omics matrix, and a phenotypic outcome (e.g., prenatal hexachlorobenzene, proteomics with list-wise/sporadic missingness, childhood BMI z-score) and want latent clusters linking them.

name: multi-omics-latent-cluster-estimation
description: Use when you need to identify latent subgroups jointly defined by an environmental exposure (e.g. maternal hexachlorobenzene), a multi-omics matrix (e.g. proteomics), and a phenotypic outcome (e.g. childhood BMI z-score), including when omics data have missing entries.

name: multi-omics-latent-factor-inference
description: Use when you have normalized expression/feature matrices for two or more omics modalities measured on the same spatial spots (e.g. spatial-CITE-seq, Stereo-CITE-seq) plus spot coordinates, and need joint dimension reduction that preserves spatial correlation for domain detection.

name: multi-omics-method-benchmarking-extraction
description: Use when an article compares several mechanistic/pathway modeling tools across fixed property axes (omics data types, Boolean PKN flags such as Ser/Thr Kinome Atlas integration, algorithm class) and you need a machine-readable comparison table.

name: multi-omics-power-analysis
description: Use when designing a multi-omic experiment (e.g. RNA-seq, miRNA-seq, DNase-seq, metabolomics) and you need the optimal number of replicates per omic to reach target per-omic and average power at a given FDR and Cohen's d.

name: multi-omics-program-discovery
description: Use when starting mosaic integration of datasets with mismatched features or modalities, and each dataset must first be factorized independently into programs across a range of resolutions before cross-dataset integration.

name: multi-omics-protein-activity-inference
description: Use when matched case/control transcriptomics, proteomics, and phosphoproteomics tables are available and the goal is an unbiased activity score (mf/final_score) per signaling protein before network reconstruction or phenotyping.

name: multi-omics-sample-size-estimation
description: Use when designing a multi-omic experiment and you must size the cohort: MultiPower for differential-feature power across omics, or MultiML when a classifier such as random forest must hit a target classification error rate (e.g., ER=0.01) on combined omic platforms.

name: multi-omics-scatter-visualization
description: Use when you have high-dimensional abundance matrices (e.g., 2348 LC-MS metabolites x 182 isolates, 1541 GC-MS volatiles x 182 isolates) and need to visually assess whether samples cluster by a categorical annotation such as bacterial taxonomy.

name: multi-omics-statistical-annotation-overlay
description: Use when you have fold-change (z-score) and p-value matrices — or a pathway/feature grid table — for multi-omics or time-course data and need a publication-quality heatmap with embedded statistical annotations.

name: multi-rank-resolution-sampling
description: Use when you have a normalized expression matrix (bulk RNA-Seq, MS proteomics, or snRNA-Seq) with over-dispersed features already selected, and you need unbiased program anchors spanning coarse to fine resolutions rather than a single fixed k.

name: multi-resolution-conditional-independence-testing
description: Use when running VI-VS on single-cell count data (e.g. PBMC with a scanpy AnnData of raw counts) and you want to report discoveries at multiple feature granularities (e.g. 200-, 300-cluster and per-gene) with calibrated FDR and power per resolution.

name: multi-view-feature-augmentation
description: Use when preparing spatial transcriptomics data (AnnData with normalized expression matrix plus spot coordinates) for a multi-view graph contrastive model, and you need >=2 expression views and >=2 adjacency matrices from different similarity criteria.

name: multiassayexperiment-data-import
description: Use when a multi-omics dataset stored as a MuData .h5mu file (e.g. PBMC RNA+ATAC) must be read into R as MultiAssayExperiment or Seurat objects, preserving shared cell barcodes across modalities.

name: multilayer-edge-annotation-parsing
description: Use when you have run RWR_ShortestPaths against an RWRtoolkit multiplex (e.g. the 9-layer comprehensive A. thaliana network, delta = 0.5) and need to parse, validate, or summarize the returned edge list records for all source-target pairs.

name: multimodal-container-serialization
description: Use when single-cell count matrices from multiple modalities (e.g. RNA + ATAC from Cell Ranger outputs or a snap file) must be combined into one interoperable file and exchanged across languages or tools.

name: multimodal-factor-analysis
description: Use when paired multi-omics single-cell data (e.g. 10x PBMC Chromium Single Cell Multiome ATAC + Gene Expression in filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5) needs unsupervised integration into shared latent factors spanning both RNA and ATAC modalities.

name: multimodal-gene-expression-image-integration
description: Use when analyzing 10x Visium-style spatial transcriptomics data (count matrix + spatial coordinates + H&E image) and you want to test whether morphological image features improve spatial domain clustering (ARI) over expression-only baselines.

name: multimodal-integration-of-spatial-omics
description: Use when a Visium/ST dataset has H&E image data with informative morphology (e.g. DLPFC layers or HER2 tumor regions) and you need joint gene+image+space spot clusters to compare against manual annotations.

name: multimodal-wnn-integration
description: Use when spot-level ST data have been normalized (SCT) with image features extracted (VGG16/RGB via LoadImageFeature) and you need spot clustering that jointly weighs gene expression and histology modality after a spatially aware process.

name: multiomics-mofa-factor-analysis
description: Use when a MuData object contains observations measured across two or more modalities (RNA + ATAC multiome, or CITE-seq RNA + protein) and a joint, interpretable latent space or joint embedding is needed for visualisation and cell-type-level interpretation.

name: multiomics-object-routing-to-visualization-classes
description: Use when you hold multi-omics input in mixed shapes — a raw expression/count matrix, a precomputed DE table (log2fc, negLog10p), or a MultiAssayExperiment object — and want one call to auto-route it to the correct volcano/heatmap class without manually choosing a plotting class.

name: multiple-testing-correction-calculation
description: Use when performing power calculations over many omic features where a target FDR (e.g. alpha = 0.05) must be controlled: the per-test significance level must be shrunk from nominal alpha to alpha before computing power or optimal sample size.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-bonferroni-tuning
description: Use when running Scoary2 associations between a pan-genome gene presence/absence matrix and numeric multi-omics traits and you must choose between strict FDR-BH filtering and a relaxed trait-wise Bonferroni correction to recover candidate genes.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-power-calculation
description: Use when designing or evaluating a multi-omic differential-features study and you need a per-platform replicate number that meets target per-omic and average power under an FDR threshold, e.g. omicPower 0.6, averagePower 0.8, FDR 0.05.

name: multiple-testing-pvalue-correction
description: Use when calling RBP target transcripts from differential RNA-editing statistics where thousands of 50-nt transcript bins are tested simultaneously and raw Poisson P values would inflate false target calls.

name: multiplex-network-construction
description: Use when you have multiple edge-list files representing distinct relationship types (e.g. coexpression, PPI, regulation layers) and need a single multiplex network object with supra-adjacency and transition matrices for RWR analysis.

name: multiplex-network-cross-validation
description: Use when a constructed multiplex network needs statistical evaluation of whether curated gene sets (e.g., MAPMAN- or GO-derived) show topological similarity sufficient to recover held-out genes via random walk with restart.

name: multiplex-network-gene-set-evaluation
description: Use when a curated gene set (e.g. shared MAPMAN or GO annotation) must be validated for functional/topological connectivity in a preassembled multiplex network before using it for ranking or discovery.

name: multiplex-network-random-walk-scoring
description: Use when you have a set of seed genes (e.g. from a pathway or GWAS) and a preassembled or custom multiplex network (multiple omic layers), and need ranked topological context around the seeds.

name: multiplex-network-shortest-path-extraction
description: Use when you have a prebuilt multiplex network (RData) and two gene-set files, and you need the concrete shortest paths and path lengths connecting every source-target gene pair.

name: multiplex-network-statistics-extraction
description: Use when a multiplex network object (.Rdata from RWR_make_multiplex or a preassembled multiplex) needs characterization: per-layer node/edge counts and between-layer edge overlap (Jaccard) before running RWR analyses.

name: multivariable-normal-expression-generation
description: Use when benchmarking ST integration/clustering methods (e.g. stImage vs MUSE-style baselines) requires synthetic two-modality data with known ground-truth labels, controlled cluster counts, and controlled expression dropout.

name: multivariate-normal-parameter-estimation
description: Use when fitting a LUCID integrative clustering model where the omics block Z is modeled as cluster-specific multivariate normals and some rows have list-wise (or sporadic) missing omics that must not contaminate mu_j and Sigma_j updates.

name: multiview-representation-fusion
description: Use when two or more modality-specific spatial embeddings (expression, spatial adjacency, morphological image) sharing the same n_spots dimension must be combined into one (n_spots x d) unified embedding with learned per-spot attention weights.

name: mutational-signature-frequency-analysis
description: Use when somatic mutation catalogues and copy-number segment data are available per sample with a binary group assignment (e.g., low vs high iMLGAM risk score) and the goal is to test whether mutational signatures, pathway activities, or focal amplifications are directionally enriched in one group.

name: negative-control-protein-calibration-assessment
description: Use when testing a feature-selection or association method (e.g., VI-VS vs OLS) on CITE-seq gene-protein data and you need a negative-control (isotype) benchmark plus per-protein association counts to judge calibration at a fixed target FDR.

name: negative-log-likelihood-importance-scoring
description: Use when computing CRT test statistics for conditional independence testing in VI-VS: after generating synthetic feature replicates, to score observed vs. synthetic data on a held-out validation split.

name: neighborhood-graph-construction-with-neighbor-pruning
description: Use when preparing normalized transcriptome/proteome AnnData for SSGATE: per-omics KNN graphs (e.g. k_cutoff=15 on X_pca) or radius graphs must be built and Leiden-pruned before training.

name: nes-table-export-and-interpretation
description: Use when representative programs (e.g. community-representative programs from an integrated mosaicMPI network) need functional validation against curated gene sets, and NES values must be tabulated per program-by-gene-set pair.

name: network-graph-file-serialization
description: Use when a flux-scored edge list and the GGN from pyPARAGON's PageRank-flux step are ready and the tau-scaled edge subset has been selected, requiring the final context-specific network C(VC, EC) to be written to a GraphML file.

name: network-input-perturbation-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify robustness of a validated biomolecular regulatory network model under small input perturbations, using SEM of cell fate outcomes against a 0.05 SEM threshold.

name: network-node-edge-count-verification
description: Use when a multiplex network RData object (e.g. from RWR_make_multiplex with delta=0.5) must be validated after construction or reload, by checking that Pool_of_Nodes and aggregated edge counts match expected totals.

name: network-node-symbol-filtering
description: Use when patient RNA-seq data keyed by Ensembl IDs must be aligned to a fixed literature-derived biomolecular network node list before model annotation, with alias resolution for non-matching symbols.

name: network-parameter-benchmarking
description: Use when a mechanistic network reconstruction step has many tunable technical parameters (PKN source, max path lengths, ILP solver settings) and you must screen combinations, rank resulting networks by a combined score, and benchmark them against a gold-standard protein set.

name: network-permutation-significance-testing
description: Use when you must decide which subnetwork edges are statistically enriched around a seed node set — e.g., trimming a large reference interactome to significant graphlets before propagation or edge inference.

name: network-propagation-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing network propagation or context-specific subnetwork inference tools against a curated pathway gold standard (e.g., NetPath nodes and edges) across multiple reference interactomes.

name: network-rewiring-permutation-testing
description: Use when you have a curated gold-standard gene set collection (e.g., 25 MAPMAN-derived gene sets) and a multiplex network, and you need a statistical null to show RWR_CV AUROC exceeds what rewired controls give.

name: network-topology-analysis
description: Use when you have a preassembled multiplex network (e.g. the 9-layer comprehensive Arabidopsis thaliana multiplex, unweighted, delta = 0.5) and two gene sets, and you need the actual shortest-path edge lists and path lengths between every source-target pair.

name: neural-network-confidence-variability-scoring
description: Use when an annotated AnnData (e.g. PBMC scRNA-seq with an 'label' observation) must be audited for annotation mismatches, since training-dynamics confidence/variability scores expose likely erroneous annotations.

name: neural-network-hyperparameter-configuration
description: Use when training SSGATE's dual-path GATE on paired transcriptome/proteome AnnData objects and you need the paper's concrete defaults (hidden 128, out 30, 300 epochs, lr 0.001, sigma 0.1).

name: neural-network-probability-trajectory-monitoring
description: Use when an annotated single-cell AnnData object (e.g. mSTZ islet cells labeled by condition) must be audited for annotation mismatches, or when per-cell trainability scores are needed to relate labels to continuous biology like β cell activity.

name: nextflow-module-implementation
description: Use when a new analytical step must be added to a Nextflow/nf-core pipeline as an isolated, containerised process with defined inputs, channels, and outputs (e.g. a variant-extraction module in eduomics).

name: nextflow-pipeline-execution-with-containers
description: Use when a task requires launching a multi-step nf-core/DSL2 workflow such as eduomics, and reproducible, containerised execution (per-process containers) on a target compute infrastructure is needed.

name: nextflow-process-module-development
description: Use when a new nf-core/eduomics process must be added — e.g. parsing a simulated variant record in reference format to extract the gene name of an injected pathogenic variant for variant-calling meta.

name: nextflow-subworkflow-reconstruction
description: Use when a Nextflow DNA simulation pipeline must subset reference genome and known-variant resources to a target chromosome plus padded exome capture regions before read simulation.

name: nf-core-pipeline-execution-and-validation
description: Use when a task requires launching an nf-core/eduomics Nextflow workflow with a samplesheet and reference config, or validating that simulated -omics outputs pass the pipeline's internal validation module before reuse.

name: niche-cell-colocalization-analysis
description: Use when you have an annotated image-based spatial omics dataset (e.g., MERSCOPE) with cell-type labels and niche assignments, and you need to test whether specific cell populations co-localize with particular tissue niches.

name: niche-celltype-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when spatial niches have been clustered from image embeddings (e.g., H&E ResNet patches) and you need to interpret them via cell-type enrichment and protein/marker specificity (e.g., TROP2, TM4SF4, APCDD1).

name: niche-polygon-vectorization
description: Use when you have a segmented SpatialData object with cells already assigned to spatial niches/cell-type groups and need polygons plus geometric statistics (area, perimeter, roundness, occurrence) per niche compartment.

name: normal-cancer-sample-merging
description: Use when TCGA-LUSC RNA-seq gene expression data plus patient-specific CNV/SM/SV annotations must be split into paired (49), unpaired (50 normal / 453 cancer), or cancer-only (453) use cases, merged, and 0-1 normalized before CanSeer drug-score computation.

name: normalization-method-comparison
description: Use when you must verify that a spatial multi-omics dimension-reduction/clustering pipeline's results (e.g., ARI of spatial domain detection) are stable across preprocessing choices such as normalization method and gene-set selection.

name: nsclc-squamous-cell-line-annotation
description: Use when a CanSeer therapeutic-screening analysis requires GDSC2 IC50 values for candidate drugs restricted to Lung NSCLC squamous cell carcinoma cell lines, with per-drug means computed after outlier removal.

name: null-simulation-pvalue-uniformity-checking
description: Use when validating that a CRT-style conditional independence testing pipeline produces valid, calibrated p-values before applying it to real single-cell data.

name: numeric-trait-binarization-for-mgwas
description: Use when the phenotype to associate with a bacterial pan-genome is measured on a continuous scale (e.g. metabolome or other numeric omics values per isolate) and a binary gene-present/gene-absent association test is required.

name: numerical-metadata-pearson-correlation
description: Use when a community-by-sample usage matrix from mosaicMPI integration must be associated with numerical metadata layers (tumor purity, continuous scores) across samples to characterize landscape communities.

name: numerical-reference-value-reproduction
description: Use when reimplementing a published scoring pipeline (CanSeer NDAS/drug scores) and reported reference values must be reproduced numerically as an output-matches-reference validation check.

name: ols-vs-vivs-importance-score-comparison
description: Use when comparing feature-importance scorers for conditional independence testing on count-valued omics data, especially when the response is generated with non-Gaussian (Poisson) noise and FDR calibration must be verified.

name: omic-seed-node-integration
description: Use when you have a weighted seed-node (omic-hits) set (e.g., phosphoproteomic hits from tumors) plus a reference interactome with edge confidence scores, and need to propagate seed signals and score GGN edges to prioritize interactions for context-specific subnetwork reconstruction.

name: omics-missingness-simulation
description: Use when a LUCID analysis involves sporadically missing omics entries where complete-case analysis is infeasible, and you need evidence that integrated EM-based imputation outperforms mean imputation before trusting downstream cluster estimates.

name: omics-network-propagation
description: Use when you have a set of significant omic hits (e.g., phosphoproteomic seed nodes from 105 breast cancer tumors) and a reference interactome, and need sample-specific networks plus functional modules for stratification.

name: omics-pilot-data-preparation
description: Use when running MultiPower or MultiML sample-size/power estimation, since both algorithms require properly preprocessed pilot datasets per omic platform before the estimation procedure can run.

name: oncogene-tumor-suppressor-role-adjusted-scoring
description: Use when a patient-normalized expression table and per-drug target gene annotations (oncogene vs tumor suppressor) with tissue mean IC50 values must be combined into quantitative drug activity scores.

name: optimal-sample-size-estimation
description: Use when designing a multi-omic study (or evaluating an existing one) and you need the number of samples required to reach a target power for differential feature detection across two or more omic platforms, given pilot data.

name: orthogroup-locus-synteny-analysis
description: Use when Scoary2 (or Scoary) mGWAS hits need genomic-context validation — e.g. checking whether trait-associated orthogenes are adjacent, syntenic, or disrupted (transposases/frameshifts) in positive vs. negative isolates.

name: overdispersed-feature-guided-deconvolution
description: Use when each modality (bulk RNA-Seq, MS proteomics, snRNA-Seq) has been normalized and overdispersed features selected, and unbiased low- to high-resolution molecular programs are needed within each dataset prior to integration.

name: overdispersion-score-calculation
description: Use when feature selection for factorization is needed on normalized count or intensity matrices (bulk RNA-Seq, proteomics, snRNA-Seq) whose statistical properties do not fit cNMF's Poisson scRNA-Seq model, so overdispersed features must be found via mean-variance curve fitting per modality.

name: overlapping-patch-tiling-strategy
description: Use when segmenting large spatial omics images (e.g. Xenium, MERSCOPE, CosMX) with millions of cells where whole-image Cellpose or whole-transcript Baysor runs exhaust RAM or wall-clock time.

name: p-value-combination-method-taxonomy
description: Use when an analysis requires choosing or cataloguing a method to combine p-values or z-scores (independent or correlated, e.g. GWAS SNPs), or when comparing method coverage across p-value combination packages.

name: package-extdata-test-harness-execution
description: Use when validating an R/Bioconductor visualization package against its bundled example (extdata) inputs — raw matrices, precomputed DE tables, MAE objects — to confirm input-type dispatch and returned object types.

name: package-feature-comparison-matrix-construction
description: Use when you need to quantify and compare the feature/method coverage of overlapping software packages against a canonical list of methods enumerated in an article's methods table or tool documentation.

name: paga-graph-abstraction-trajectory-inference
description: Use when an SSGATE-integrated spatial AnnData (e.g. SCS_MT mouse thymus with Leiden labels) must be ordered into an anatomical trajectory (outer cortex → inner medulla) and checked against Monocle 3 pseudo-time.

name: pagerank-flux-edge-scoring
description: Use when a weighted seed-node (omic-hits) set must be propagated over a confidence-scored reference interactome with PPR and edges prioritized by flux scores, e.g. before subnetwork reconstruction on a graphlet-guided network (GGN).

name: paired-autoencoder-reconstruction-optimization
description: Use when two paired, expression-matched AnnData objects (e.g., transcriptome and proteome, single-cell or spatial) each carrying a pruned neighborhood graph in adata.uns['nbrs_net'] must be fused into a single low-dimensional joint representation.

name: paired-observation-alignment
description: Use when two score vectors cover the same methods/entities measured under different conditions or modalities and you must drop methods missing in either modality before computing a paired correlation.

name: paired-t-test-significance-testing
description: Use when comparing the clustering performance (AMI) of two methods evaluated on the same matched set of datasets or simulation replicates — e.g., 12 paired section-level AMI values — and you need a p-value for whether the improvement is statistically significant.

name: paired-transcriptome-proteome-data-preprocessing
description: Use when you have paired RNA + protein measurements in anndata/h5ad format (e.g., CITE-seq or BMNC/SLN111_D1 style data) that must be normalized into consistent formats, dimensions, units, and normalizations before integration with methods like SSGATE.

name: pairwise-comparison-algorithm-reproduction
description: Use when validating or reproducing a runtime/complexity benchmark between a reimplemented algorithm and its predecessor — specifically when timing Scoary2's pairwise-comparison code against original Scoary on synthetic gene-by-genome presence/absence matrices of varying dimensions.

name: pan-cancer-genomic-association-analysis
description: Use when TCGA pan-cancer somatic mutation, copy-number segment, and per-sample iMLGAM risk-score data are available and the goal is to test whether genomic features differ by risk-score group.

name: pan-genome-phenotype-association
description: Use when a study must link measured phenotypes (e.g. omics traits such as yogurt metabolites) to orthologous gene families (orthogroups from OrthoFinder or Roary) across dozens to hundreds of bacterial isolates using mGWAS.

name: pan-genome-presence-absence-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic pan-genome presence/absence matrices to measure how an mGWAS pairwise-comparison algorithm's runtime scales with n_genes × n_genomes, or to reproduce Scoary2's reported ~30x speedup over Scoary.

name: pangenome-neighborhood-reconstruction
description: Use when Scoary2/pan-GWAS candidate orthogenes must be validated in genomic context: e.g. checking whether correlated genes sit adjacent to known pathway loci (caiA/caiABC, fixABCX) and whether gene-negative isolates carry pseudogene disruptions.

name: par-clip-cross-validation-overlap
description: Use when you have a MAPIT-seq differential editing statistics table (e.g., RBP_Edit_GE_RPE_DATA.tsv from the callediting/calltargets steps) and want to reproduce or validate the target list against an orthogonal RBP-binding dataset such as PAR-CLIP.

name: parallel-benchmark-timing-comparison
description: Use when a package update claims to parallelize a previously sequential construction or computation step and you must quantify the speedup (e.g. multiplex network construction time for large L-layer networks).

name: parameter-estimate-bias-and-variance-assessment
description: Use when evaluating whether an imputation or analysis method yields unbiased, low-variance latent-clustering parameter estimates on incomplete multi-omics data with known ground-truth simulation parameters.

name: parameter-grid-benchmarking-against-gold-standard
description: Use when tuning a multi-omics activity-inference pipeline (e.g., SignalingProfiler 2.0) against a curated gold-standard protein/TF activity list to pick default parameters before applying the tool to new datasets.

name: parameter-grid-evaluation
description: Use when a power-calculation or correction formula depends on several scalar parameters (e.g., feature count m, DE features m1, expected true detections r1, target FDR alpha) and you need its value over all combinations rather than a single point estimate.

name: parameter-grid-search-tuning
description: Use when benchmarking a network-inference or propagation tool against current competitors and each tool's parameters must be optimized fairly over shared seed gene sets and reference interactomes before scoring recall/precision.

name: parameter-scan-gold-standard-benchmarking
description: Use when a network inference pipeline exposes tunable parameters (e.g., PhenoScore switches, ProxPath path_length, zscore_threshold) and a reference phenotype activity profile exists to judge which setting highest-ranked recapitulates expected phenotype signs.

name: pathogenic-variant-detection-verification
description: Use when simulated DNA reads carry injected ClinVar pathogenic variants and you must verify, via variant calling against a reference bundle, that the ground-truth variant is recovered before releasing the dataset for teaching.

name: pathway-activation-zscore-heatmap-encoding
description: Use when you have a pathway/feature summary table with activation z-scores, p-values, and gene counts per condition (e.g., brain region × timepoint) and need a single publication-quality heatmap that jointly visualizes all three statistics.

name: patient-cluster-module-annotation
description: Use when patient-cluster-specific inferred subnetworks need functional interpretation: Louvain modules must be tested for KEGG over-representation, pathway frequencies tabulated per cluster, or a Ras-signaling module extracted.

name: patient-stratification-clustering
description: Use when you have per-patient omic hits (e.g. significant phosphoproteins from CPTAC breast cancer tumors) plus a reference interactome, and the goal is to group patients by network-derived functional similarity rather than raw feature clustering.

name: pca-clustering-alignment-verification
description: Use when validating that simulated bulk RNA-seq/ATAC-seq count matrices reproduce the intended temporal expression patterns and experimental design before downstream GRN or correlation assessments.

name: pca-dimension-reduction-single-cell
description: Use when a single-cell CITE-seq or SMAGE-seq count matrix needs a linear low-dimensional embedding before UMAP visualization, clustering, or as SMOPCA's downstream input.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when spot-level image (or other) features are high-dimensional vectors (e.g., 2048-d CNN outputs per spatial transcriptomics spot) and a low-dimensional latent space is needed before feeding an MLP or fusion model.

name: pca-transcriptome-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when preparing single-cell or spatially resolved transcriptome data for SSGATE neighborhood-graph construction: the expression matrix in anndata.X is high-dimensional and a 'X_pca' feature matrix must exist before calling Cal_Nbrs_Net.

name: peak-memory-monitoring
description: Use when benchmarking how a simulation method's runtime or peak memory scales with the number of cells (100-10,000) or genes (500-10,000), e.g. to flag quadratic or super-quadratic complexity before applying the method at full-dataset size.

name: pearson-correlation-across-benchmark-modalities
description: Use when a benchmark table contains paired per-method performance scores computed on two data modalities (e.g., SRT vs scRNA-seq reference datasets) and the goal is to test cross-modality agreement of method rankings via Pearson correlation.

name: pearson-correlation-expression-interaction-analysis
description: Use when a cell×gene interaction-score matrix (e.g., MAPIT scores) is co-profiled with single-cell transcriptome data and you need per-gene correlation of binding strength with expression across subpopulations defined by cell cycle or clustering.

name: penalized-pspline-regression
description: Use when estimating the sample size a machine learning classifier needs on multi-omic data to reach a user-specified target classification error rate, from an ER-vs-sample-size table.

name: per-cell-channel-intensity-quantification
description: Use when image-based spatial omics data (Xenium, CosMX, MACSima, PhenoCycler) contains protein-staining channels and per-cell intensity values are needed for cell-type annotation or niche enrichment analysis.

name: per-method-error-rate-quantification
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq or SRT simulation methods and you need to know which methods raise execution errors, how often, and in which error categories (e.g. failed parameter estimation, missing/infinite values).

name: percentile-based-parameter-estimation
description: Use when designing a multi-omic experiment and you need MultiPower input parameters estimated from pilot data: a count matrix per omic plus a Cohen's d threshold d0 are available, and sample size will be computed via optimalRep(parameters, ...).

name: permuted-cluster-background-statistics
description: Use when validating de novo motif discovery on MAPIT-seq edit clusters: you need a matched control background (permuted clusters in the same genes) to compute fold enrichment of a known motif such as UGCAUG against HOMER output.

name: personalized-pagerank-network-propagation
description: Use when a weighted set of omic hit proteins must be propagated over a reference interactome to re-score all proteins and prioritize edges by directional PageRank-flux before selecting a context-specific subnetwork.

name: perturbed-graph-negative-sampling
description: Use when training a self-supervised graph convolutional encoder (e.g., MCGAE's Eq. 2 DGI contrastive objective) on spatial transcriptomics graphs and negative examples are needed for the contrastive loss.

name: pheno-network-phenotype-activity-inference
description: Use when a validated context-specific network (nodes_df, edges_df, igraph) must be linked to cellular phenotypes and phenotype activities inferred from upstream protein activities, as in benchmarking 96 PhenoScore/ProxPath parameter conditions against a phenotypic gold standard.

name: phenotype-activity-scoring-phenoscore
description: Use when a SignalingProfiler 2.0 context-specific network exists and you must quantify which cellular phenotypes are significantly activated or inhibited by the perturbation, using upstream protein activity scores.

name: phenotype-trait-binarization
description: Use when a trait table contains continuous (numeric) phenotype columns that must be dichotomized for a binary GWAS tool such as Scoary2, and isolates with ambiguous trait classification should be excluded rather than forced into a class.

name: phosphoproteomic-activity-inference-method-taxonomy
description: Use when a paper presents or cites multiple mechanistic network-inference tools (e.g. SignalingProfiler 2.0, COSMOS, CausalPath, CARNIVAL, HiPathia, NicheNet, KPNN) and a side-by-side property comparison table must be filled from text.

name: phosphoproteomics-data-preprocessing
description: Use when starting a SignalingProfiler 2.0 analysis from phosphoproteomic data and you need to verify or reformat the input table (one row per phosphosite, required identifier/differential columns) before footprint-based or PhosphoScore inference.

name: phosphosite-mapping-on-network-edges
description: Use when a two-shots CARNIVAL-optimized signaling network (union_of_graphs output, SIF + RDS) must be supported by measured phosphoproteomics — i.e., each retained signaling edge needs its matched phosphosite, fold-change and significance annotation before downstream phenoscore or benchmarking.

name: phosphosite-regulatory-activity-scoring
description: Use when a phosphoproteomic table (case vs control log-ratios per phosphosite) must be converted into protein-level activity scores for kinases, phosphatases, and other phosphorylated proteins via regulatory phosphosite annotations.

name: pkn-filtering-by-quantified-analytes
description: Use when starting SignalingProfiler 2.0 Step 2 with multi-omics tables and a full prior knowledge network: the PKN must first be subset to analytes measured in transcriptomics, proteomics, and phosphoproteomics before receptor-to-TF path construction.

name: poisson-count-response-simulation
description: Use when validating FDR calibration of a conditional-independence/variable-selection method (e.g., VI-VS vs OLS) on semi-synthetic single-cell count data whose response is generated from a Poisson, not Gaussian, noise model.

name: poisson-editing-site-filtering
description: Use when calling RBP target transcripts from MAPIT-seq RNA editing event tables (e.g. _Edit__DATA.tsv from callediting) and noisy editing sites must be pruned by Poisson p-value before differential enrichment testing.

name: polygon-chunk-spatial-intersection
description: Use when a segmentation produced cell polygons over a large on-disk multi-channel image and per-cell channel intensities must be averaged without loading the whole image into memory.

name: posterior-inclusion-probability-visualization
description: Use when a fitted LUCIDus model (e.g., HCB exposure, incomplete proteomics, childhood BMI z-score) yields bootstrap-based posterior inclusion probabilities and you need to visualize and interpret variable inclusion uncertainty.

name: posterior-responsibility-computation
description: Use when fitting a LUCID latent unknown clustering model on exposures (G), omics data (Z), and outcome (Y) where the EM algorithm must assign each observation a posterior probability of belonging to each latent cluster, especially when sporadic or list-wise missing omics values must be imputed

name: power-analysis-methods
description: Use when designing or evaluating a differential-analysis experiment over many omic features (RNA-seq, proteomics, etc.) and you must compute the per-test alpha adjusted for a target FDR, or estimate optimal replicate numbers.

name: power-curve-visualization
description: Use when a multi-omic power analysis (MultiPower) has been run with optimalRep()/postMultiPower() and power-vs-sample-size curves are needed per omic and for average power to justify the chosen sample size.

name: power-curve-visualization-across-omics
description: Use when a multi-omics pilot dataset has been processed with MultiPower/optimalRep and per-omic power or detectable Cohen's d trade-off curves are needed to inspect or communicate optimal sample sizes.

name: prc2-rna-substrate-validation
description: Use when validating RBP target calls from MAPIT-seq editing data — specifically reproducing or extending near-empty PRC2 component target sets (EED, EZH2, SUZ12) and verifying XIST adjusted P values.

name: precision-recall-driver-recovery-scoring
description: Use when evaluating how well a network reconstruction method recovers known driver genes (e.g., IntOGen) from mutated-gene seed sets, requiring precision/recall comparison against baseline methods under k-fold cross-validation.

name: precision-recall-rmse-evaluation
description: Use when a multi-omics inference pipeline (e.g. SignalingProfiler 2.0 Step 1) has been run under multiple parameter or resource conditions and you must quantify recovery of known gold-standard protein activities via precision, recall, and RMSE.

name: prediction-error-importance-scoring
description: Use when you have an existing feature-importance or network-inference method (e.g., GENIE3) whose raw discoveries lack calibration, and you need theoretically valid, FDR-controlled decisions on single-cell expression data.

name: prior-knowledge-network-assembly
description: Use when building or updating the causal prior knowledge network that SignalingProfiler's Step 2 (CARNIVAL network reconstruction) consumes, or when assembling a custom PKN from SIGNOR/PsP/OmniPath resources.

name: prior-knowledge-network-property-annotation
description: Use when building a feature-by-feature comparison of pathway/mechanistic modeling tools (e.g., SignalingProfiler 2.0, COSMOS, CARNIVAL, HiPathia, CausalPath) and you must populate per-tool cells for omics data types and PKN properties.

name: prior-segmentation-integration-for-patchify
description: Use when re-segmenting MERSCOPE or Xenium spatial-transcriptomics data with Baysor inside Sopa and a vendor or Cellpose segmentation is available to pass as a prior via prior_shapes_key.

name: probability-normalization-and-confidence-thresholding
description: Use when a Bayesian protein-recovery run has produced raw presence probabilities for unobserved proteins and you must normalize scores across samples and apply a confidence cutoff (0.50–0.95, default 0.95) before reporting recovered proteins.

name: program-anchor-edge-list-construction
description: Use when factorized program matrices (e.g. .h5ad from task_002 cNMF runs over CPTAC datasets) must be linked into anchor edges for mosaic integration, with per-dataset-pair correlation thresholds.

name: program-feature-score-matrix-handling
description: Use when an integrated mosaicMPI network (e.g. network_integration.pkl.gz) exists and community-representative programs must be exported and scored against gene sets (GMT) to validate community labels such as T-cell or vasculature programs.

name: program-feature-score-pearson-correlation
description: Use when integrating cNMF-factorized program feature-score matrices (.h5ad) from cohorts with incomplete molecular-feature overlap, and you need anchored, highly correlated program pairs to build a cross-dataset program network.

name: program-network-community-detection
description: Use when a thresholded program-level correlation/anchor network (e.g. GraphML + pearson.df.npz) exists and you need to partition programs across datasets/modalities into communities for downstream annotation transfer.

name: protein-abundance-distribution-visualisation
description: Use when CITE-seq 'Antibody capture' counts have been dsb-normalised and you need to inspect per-epitope abundance distributions before defining cell types or integrating protein with gene expression.

name: protein-complex-curation
description: Use when building or expanding a protein complex reference panel from heterogeneous sources (CORUM, STRING, Complex Portal, Reactome) for network-based protein recovery or co-complex analyses.

name: protein-complex-network-inference
description: Use when a proteomics expression matrix (rows: UniProt proteins, columns: samples) has persistent missing values and the goal is to predict which absent-but-expected proteins are biologically present using complex co-membership evidence.

name: protein-complex-prior-harmonization
description: Use when benchmarking protein recovery methods on a shared expression matrix and you must remove prior-knowledge asymmetry — e.g. testing whether Protrec2's advantage derives from its Bayesian inference rather than its expanded 3,885-complex multi-source prior.

name: protein-complex-prior-probability-computation
description: Use when preparing Protrec2 inputs: you must convert curated complex records (updated_tissue_complex_.csv) into per-tissue prior probabilities across the 27 supported tissues before Bayesian recovery.

name: protein-expression-direction-consistency-analysis
description: Use when recovered/predicted missing proteins from tumor-normal proteomic data (e.g., Protrec2 per-sample probability CSVs binarized at 0.50-0.95 cutoffs) must be checked for direction consistency against independent cohort expression (e.g., CPTAC PDC000234/PDC000153).

name: protein-interaction-network-scoring
description: Use when a weighted seed-node set (omic-hits) must be propagated over a reference interactome via Personalized PageRank and edges prioritized by flux scores for context-specific subnetwork reconstruction.

name: protein-interaction-score-distribution-visualization
description: Use when comparing discovery sets from conditional dependency tests (e.g., VI-VS at 10% target FDR) against a baseline like OLS on gene-protein data, and you want to assess biological plausibility via StringDB combined-score distributions.

name: protein-missing-value-recovery
description: Use when a DDA proteomics expression matrix (rows = proteins, columns = samples) contains missing proteins and you need probabilistic presence predictions validated against an independent reference (e.g. diaPASEF, Astral, CPTAC).

name: protein-network-community-annotation
description: Use when you have a context-specific subnetwork (e.g., pyPARAGON patient-cluster-specific networks from 105 breast cancer tumors) and need functional modules with over-represented pathways or biological processes for stratification-level interpretation.

name: protein-recovery-probability-estimation
description: Use when a proteomics expression matrix (rows = proteins, columns = samples) has missing proteins you want to recover as per-sample probability scores, especially with matched tumor-normal samples and a known tissue of origin.

name: proteomics-expression-matrix-formatting
description: Use when preparing a protein-by-sample abundance table (e.g., from DDA-PASEF or Astral runs) for Protrec2 recovery, or when a CSV fails because protein IDs or the rows/columns layout do not match the expected format.

name: proteomics-recovery-rate-benchmarking
description: Use when you have a DDA/DIA proteomics expression matrix (rows: UniProt proteins, columns: samples) with missing proteins and an external validation protein set, and need to quantify how many unreported-but-present proteins each recovery method correctly predicts.

name: proxpath-phenotype-proximity-scoring
description: Use when a validated context-specific signaling network (nodes/edges from Step 2) must be linked to cellular phenotypes, and phenotype activation/deactivation signs need to be inferred from upstream protein activities.

name: pseudo-differential-feature-selection
description: Use when a preprocessed, batch-effect-free pilot multi-omic count matrix is available and you need to derive MultiPower inputs (variability/PSD percentile, effect size, number of variables) for optimal sample-size estimation.

name: pseudo-spatial-coordinate-generation-for-single-cell-multiomics
description: Use when applying a spatial model (e.g., SMOPCA) to single-cell multi-omics count matrices that have no physical coordinates and you need pseudo-spatial locations derived from the transcriptomic latent space.

name: pseudo-spatial-coordinate-simulation-on-2d-grid
description: Use when benchmarking spatially aware multi-omics dimension reduction/clustering methods (e.g. SMOPCA vs SpatialPCA, scMDC) on single-cell multi-omics datasets such as CITE-seq or SMAGE-seq count matrices that lack real spatial coordinates.

name: pseudotime-gene-expression-trend-visualization
description: Use when an SSGATE-integrated spatial AnnData with a Leiden clustering exists and the goal is to verify a spatial developmental trajectory (e.g., outer cortex to inner medulla) and its gene expression dynamics.

name: pvalue-combination-dependent-tests
description: Use when input is a text file of n rows × k columns of p-values (or z-scores) whose columns/tests are correlated (e.g. SNPs within a gene, correlated GWAS tests) and a combined p-value robust to dependence is required.

name: pyramidal-ome-tif-image-export
description: Use when a processed SpatialData object (e.g. tuto.zarr) must be opened in the Xenium Explorer and the microscopy image still needs conversion into the Explorer's pyramidal .ome.tif format.

name: r-bioconductor-heatmap-rendering
description: Use when you need to visualize pathway- or feature-level activity matrices (fold-change/z-score plus p-value and counts) as an annotated composite heatmap in R, e.g. multi-region/timepoint omics summaries.

name: r-implementation-of-mathematical-programming-models
description: Use when an R workflow must select integer decision variables (e.g., per-omic replicate counts) under linear constraints such as minimum power per technology, minimum average power, FDR, and a max.size bound.

name: r-input-type-detection
description: Use when designing or reimplementing a unified R entry-point function (like MultiModalPlot()) that must auto-detect heterogeneous input shapes—raw matrices, DE tables, MAE objects—and route them to class-specific plotting constructors.

name: r-object-serialization
description: Use when a Python-created MuData .h5mu file must be consumed in R, or when a multi-modality R object (e.g. PBMC 'rna' + 'atac') needs to be saved to .rds for reuse.

name: r-package-function-implementation
description: Use when translating a published statistical algorithm (e.g., an EM imputation update for missing omics data) into an implemented, installable R package function that end users can call on their own data.

name: r-package-scripting
description: Use when scripting an R-based consensus clustering pipeline for scRNAseq data packaged as a SingleCellExperiment object, or when extending CHAI with custom clustering algorithms via its R API.

name: r-package-statistical-workflow
description: Use when designing a multi-omics experiment and you need per-omic optimal sample sizes (optionally unconstrained, unequal sizes at equal cost) plus a sample-size vs detectable Cohen's d trade-off curve from pilot omics matrices in R.

name: r-statistical-programming
description: Use when designing high-throughput multi-omic experiments where many features are tested simultaneously and a target false discovery rate (e.g. alpha = 0.05, 0.01, 0.10) must be translated into a per-test significance level for power/sample-size calculations.

name: r-vignette-reproducible-rendering
description: Use when reference for reproducing an R package's documented example pipeline end-to-end (e.g., re-running a vignette's synthetic MultiAssayExperiment generation and plotting) and verifying that locally computed outputs match the vignette's rendered figures.

name: r-wgcna-module-detection
description: Use when benchmarking WGCNA module detection against SGCRNA on the same expression matrix, or when reproducing the SGCRNA-vs-WGCNA execution-time comparison on GSE114007 (normalizedCounts_coding.tsv).

name: r2-agreement-assessment
description: Use when two tools or methods produce comparable combined p-value sets (e.g. metacp CCT/MinP/MCM/CMC vs GWAR MIN2/MAX on the same SNPs) and you need a quantitative agreement metric on the -log10 p-value scale.

name: random-forest-classification
description: Use when designing a multi-omic classification experiment and you need to know how many samples a random forest predictor needs to achieve a fixed target error rate across single- and multi-omic feature combinations.

name: random-forest-resource-prediction
description: Use when you need to predict or characterize the computational cost (execution time, peak memory) of simulation methods across resampled dataset sizes from 100-10,000 cells and 500-10,000 genes.

name: random-walk-cross-validation-scoring
description: Use when you have a curated gene set (e.g. MAPMAN or GO terms) and a multiplex network, and want to test whether the set's members are topologically more connected than the rest of the network via RWR cross-validation.

name: random-walk-restart-gene-ranking
description: Use when a curated seed gene set (e.g., MAPMAN- or GO-derived) must be scored or validated for functional interconnectivity on a multi-layer multiplex network, and left-out genes should be ranked by RWR proximity (AUROC/AUPRC).

name: randomization-based-phenotype-significance-testing
description: Use when connecting a Step 2 context-specific network to cellular phenotypes via ProxPath and you need to prune spuriously proximal phenotypes before computing PhenoScore or re-optimizing a phenotype network with CARNIVAL.

name: ras-signaling-module-visualization
description: Use when a pyPARAGON community analysis over patient-cluster-specific breast cancer networks (105 tumors) has identified modules, and you must extract the Ras-signaling module whose intermediate nodes are KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, RHOA, and RHOD for Figure 4E-style visualization.

name: rbfox2-ugcaug-canonical-motif-validation
description: Use when high-confidence edit-cluster BED intervals from MAPIT-seq are available for an RBP (e.g., RBFOX2) and you must confirm de novo motif recovery against a known consensus like UGCAUG.

name: rbp-binding-motif-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when MAPIT-seq high-confidence edit cluster BED files (hc_cluster output) are available for an RBP such as RBFOX2 and the goal is to de novo discover or validate its canonical binding motif (UGCAUG) with fold-enrichment statistics.

name: rbp-binding-region-annotation
description: Use when MAPIT-seq alignments in Mapit_result must be converted into high-confidence RBP-binding regions via adjacent hADAR2dd (A-to-G) and rAPOBEC1 (C-to-U) edit clusters.

name: rbp-binding-target-threshold-filtering
description: Use when you have a MAPIT-seq differential editing statistics table (e.g., RBP_Edit_GE_RPE_DATA.tsv from the calltargets step) and need to define the RBP's target gene set under default thresholds.

name: rbp-target-identification
description: Use when calling RBP target transcripts from per-sample MAPIT-seq RNA editing event tables (e.g. _Edit__DATA.tsv), comparing a deaminase-expressing treatment against its control to recover bound RNAs.

name: read-pair-orientation-via-rt-primer-matching
description: Use when raw sci-L3 FASTQ read pairs arrive in unknown orientation and each read must be labeled with its SSS barcode and IVT UMI before first-round (Tn5) and second-round (ligation) barcode matching.

name: recovery-precision-metric-computation
description: Use when scoring predicted missing-protein recoveries against a reference proteome — e.g., comparing Protrec2/PROTREC/GSEA outputs by recovery rate and validated-protein counts across probability cutoffs and upper-/lower-bound scenarios.

name: recovery-rate-validation-against-reference-proteome
description: Use when a protein recovery or missing-protein prediction method outputs per-protein probabilities and you need to quantify the recovery rate against an independent reference proteome (e.g. diaPASEF, Astral HeLa) under upper- or lower-bound masking.

name: reference-bundle-subset-handling
description: Use when a DNA simulation task defines a single chromosome (e.g. chr22) and capture regions, and the GATK.GRCh38 reference plus annotation must be reduced to a chromosome-specific bundle before variant extraction or read simulation.

name: reference-dataset-benchmark-orchestration
description: Use when many (tens of) simulation or analysis methods must be run uniformly over a panel of real reference datasets in R, with per-execution error capture and per-method success/error-rate aggregation.

name: reference-genome-subsetting
description: Use when a DNA simulation must target a specific chromosome and exome capture region, and subsetting workflow needs chromosome FASTA, padded BEDs, and region-restricted variant VCFs.

name: reference-interactome-subnetwork-extraction
description: Use when given a reference interactome plus an omic-hit seed node set (e.g. phosphoproteomic hits from CPTAC breast cancer samples) and you need to prune the interactome to a seed-anchored, context-specific region before edge scoring or propagation.

name: reference-pvalue-validation-testing
description: Use when implementing or porting a statistical p-value combination method and you need to verify correctness against published reference p-values or an established tool's output on the same dataset.

name: regulator-gene-association-configuration
description: Use when building synthetic multi-omics benchmarks of multi-layer GRN inference or integration pipelines, and you must define which regulators (miRNAs, TFs, ATAC/ChIP/Methyl signals) regulate which transcripts.

name: regulator-gene-correlation-validation
description: Use when you have simulated (or benchmarked) bulk RNA-seq/ATAC-seq count matrices plus a regulator-gene association matrix and need to verify that simulated regulatory interactions show expected correlations versus no-effect pairs.

name: regulon-randomization-benchmarking
description: Use when stress-testing SignalingProfiler 2.0 predictions against degraded prior knowledge — e.g., quantifying how partially shuffled regulons (tfea/ksea) or PKN_human_dir rewirings affect Step 1 activity inference or Step 2 network reconstruction.

name: replicate-reproducibility-intersection
description: Use when you have per-replicate editing-site/cluster calls (e.g., SAILOR+FLARE output for A-to-G or C-to-U edits) and need to keep only clusters supported in every replicate before pairing edit types.

name: reproducible-r-vignette-execution
description: Use when a paper claims a vignette or scripted workflow reproduces a published result (e.g., a trans-omic network figure) and the goal is to rerun that code verbatim on the deposited data and confirm the output.

name: restriction-fragment-annotation-mboi
description: Use when sci-L3-Hi-C pairs have been filtered to UU/UR/RU valid pairs and need restriction-fragment (MboI GATC) annotation and short-distance (<= 1 kb) interaction removal prior to downstream binning or QC statistics.

name: restriction-fragment-pair-deduplication
description: Use when computing per-cell informative chromatin interaction counts from single-cell Hi-C valid-pairs/pairix records and IVT-based amplification duplicates must be removed by collapsing contacts to unique restriction-fragment combinations before reporting medians.

name: retention-time-error-assessment
description: Use when metabolite identities detected in an LC-MS metabolome (e.g. carnitine species) must be confirmed by pure-standard injection and reported as a table of m/z, CAS numbers, and mass/retention-time errors.

name: ring-gene-filtering
description: Use when a raw ST gene count matrix (e.g., H1.tsv from Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.4751624) is about to be loaded into stImage via LoadImageFeature, and ring-pattern artifact genes must be removed first.

name: risk-score-based-cohort-stratification
description: Use when a per-sample continuous risk or predictive score (e.g. iMLGAM riskscore) is available for a cohort such as TCGA and the goal is to split tumors into low/high groups and test for differential genomic determinants.

name: risk-score-stratified-group-comparison
description: Use when a cohort has per-sample risk/predictive scores from a fitted model (e.g., iMLGAM scores computed via predict(ga_fit, ...)) and you need to test whether score-defined groups differ in immune infiltration or immunogenicity metrics.

name: risk-score-validation-across-cohorts
description: Use when a continuous predictive score has been computed for immunotherapy cohorts and you must demonstrate it outperforms existing biomarkers (PD-L1, TMB) via ROC/AUC comparison across cohorts.

name: rna-editing-cluster-interval-extension
description: Use when you have a BED file of high-confidence RNA-editing clusters from the MAPIT-seq hc_cluster step and need to convert them into sequence windows for de novo RBP-binding motif discovery (e.g. testing RBFOX2 UGCAUG enrichment).

name: rna-editing-event-detection-gatk
description: Use when you have MAPIT-seq BAM alignments (post-mapping and finetuning) with hADAR2dd and rAPOBEC1 deamination and need to call adjacent A-to-G and C-to-U editing events to mark RBP-bound transcripts.

name: rna-editing-site-calling
description: Use when MAPIT-seq alignments (Mapit_result directory) are ready and you must detect C-to-U and A-to-G editing events from hADAR2dd and rAPOBEC1 to pinpoint RBP-binding regions.

name: rna-seq-count-filtering-and-normalization
description: Use when raw count matrices (e.g. MOSim-simulated RNA-seq or miRNA-seq counts, or experimental bulk counts) must be filtered for low-expression features and TMM-normalized before differential expression analysis or regulatory-network inference.

name: rna-seq-read-simulation-from-count-matrices
description: Use when you need simulated RNA-seq FASTQ data whose underlying expression counts contain a known, controlled differential expression pattern for teaching or validating DESeq2/Salmon workflows.

name: rna-seq-transcript-abundance-quantification
description: Use when starting from RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g. Polyester-simulated paired-end reads) and transcript-level abundance estimates or a gene-level count matrix are needed for differential expression analysis.

name: rna-versus-dna-read-classification
description: Use when processing sci-L3 paired-end FASTQ reads from the joint RNA/chromatin-accessibility (RNA/ATAC) co-assay, where reads must be labeled RNA or DNA so downstream splitting can separate transcriptome from accessibility data per single cell.

name: rnaseq-gene-annotation
description: Use when patient RNA-seq data is keyed by Ensembl gene IDs and must be converted to gene symbols that match nodes of a fixed network model, with unmatched symbols resolved via GeneCards/HGNC aliases.

name: robust-rank-aggregation-statistics
description: Use when comparing several integration/clustering methods across multiple datasets and metrics and you need a single, statistically defensible overall ranking rather than per-metric cherry-picking.

name: roc-auc-discrimination-assessment
description: Use when a fitted ga_fit (GA_train output) exists and you must score train/validat/test prediction matrices and quantify ICB-response discrimination with ROC-AUC per cohort.

name: roc-auc-immunotherapy-response-evaluation
description: Use when an ICB/immunotherapy response prediction score (e.g. iMLGAM riskscore) has been computed and you must verify its discriminative performance holds within individual tumor types (RCC, urothelial carcinoma, melanoma, gastric cancer, GBM) rather than only in pooled cohorts.

name: roc-curve-analysis
description: Use when continuous biomarker scores (e.g. iMLGAM riskscore, PD-L1, TMB) and binary ICB response labels ('res' column) are available per cohort and you must compare predictive performance via ROC/AUC.

name: runtime-benchmarking-of-mgwas-algorithms
description: Use when comparing the computational performance of two GWAS/association algorithms whose runtimes are expected to scale with the number of genes and genomes, and you need a reproducible speedup ratio plus a closed-form runtime formula.

name: rwr-seed-score-computation
description: Use when seed genes/nodes must be scored against a multiplex network and per-layer tau weighting should influence rankings — e.g. to verify that layer importance parameters actually change output scores.

name: s4-class-dispatch-implementation
description: Use when an R analysis must accept heterogeneous multi-omics inputs (raw expression matrix, precomputed DE table, or MultiAssayExperiment object) and one unified plotting entry point must detect the type and dispatch to the right visualization class.

name: sample-size-curve-interpretation
description: Use when MultiML (or similar) has produced predicted sample sizes (PSS) per omic-platform combination at a fixed target ER and you must validate or interpret the sample-size trend before design decisions.

name: sankey-diagram-visualization
description: Use when you have a fitted LUCID model (from lucid()/estimate_lucid()) built on an exposure matrix G, omics matrix Z, and outcome Y, and you need to communicate the G-Z-Y interplay and cluster flows visually.

name: scalability-benchmark-visualization
description: Use when selecting among simulation methods for scRNA-seq or spatially resolved transcriptomics data and you need to quantify how execution time and memory scale with the number of cells or genes before committing to a method.

name: scaling-linearity-assessment
description: Use when evaluating whether automated network rendering (e.g. transomics2cytoscape stacking n pathway layers in Cytoscape) remains feasible as the number of layers grows, by timing runs across a layer-count series.

name: scam-shape-constrained-regression
description: Use when benchmark measurements (runtime, memory) across increasing cell/gene counts need a shape-constrained regression fit to assign complexity classes and predict resource consumption of simulation methods.

name: scanpy-anndata-single-cell-data-handling
description: Use when single-cell count data (e.g., scRNA-seq) must be loaded into a scanpy AnnData object with raw counts and responses stored in obsm before fitting VIVS or similar models, or when the gene set must be reduced to a manageable size.

name: scanpy-umap-visualization-of-anndata
description: Use when an AnnData object already carries a neighbor graph in adata.obsp['connectivities'] (expression-based or confidence-based) and you need a 2D UMAP embedding colored by confidence scores or markers, e.g. to compare treatment clustering vs E/M marker gradients.

name: sci-l3-single-cell-bam-processing
description: Use when single-cell BAMs from the sci-L3-RNA/ATAC human cell mixing experiment (BJ vs HEK293T) need cell identity labels, and private-SNV VCFs (BJ from bulk WGS, HEK293T lifted to hg19) are available as the ground-truth reference.

name: scoary2-python-api-usage
description: Use when you need to call Scoary2 as a Python library (github.com/MrTomRod/scoary-2) to simulate, batch, or script pan-genome association runs — e.g. planting causal genes in simulated presence/absence matrices and extracting ranked p-values for numeric traits.

name: scrna-seq-annotation-error-detection
description: Use when an annotated scRNA-seq AnnData (cell-type labels in adata.obs['label']) is suspected to contain mislabeled cells, and you want training-dynamics-based evidence plus marker-gene verification.

name: scrna-seq-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing clustering methods on single-cell RNA-seq datasets with known cell-type labels, e.g. Baron, Zeisel, Zheng68K, or SC-Mixology, to decide which method performs highest-ranked.

name: scrna-seq-disease-condition-annotation-analysis
description: Use when a scRNA-seq AnnData object is annotated by coarse experimental condition (disease vs healthy) and you want to test whether DNN training-dynamics confidence tracks graded disease severity via marker module expression.

name: scrnaseq-clustering-ensemble-implementation
description: Use when multiple scRNAseq clustering results must be integrated into one consensus cell-assignment set via average similarity on binary matrices, with silhouette-guided k selection.

name: scrnaseq-dataset-subsampling
description: Use when you must test whether a scRNAseq clustering method's performance (e.g., ARI on Zheng68K) is robust to dataset size and cell-type complexity, by benchmarking on controlled subsampled datasets.

name: scrnaseq-srt-cross-platform-comparison
description: Use when a benchmark produces per-method accuracy scores computed separately on SRT and scRNA-seq reference datasets (e.g., accuracy_scores.csv) and you need to test cross-platform agreement of method rankings/scores.

name: sct-normalization-preprocessing
description: Use when starting stImage analysis of a Visium or ST spatial transcriptomics dataset whose raw counts (e.g. filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5) and H&E image-derived features need normalization, batch/feature filtering, and dimensionality reduction before clustering or modality integration.

name: seed-gene-network-propagation
description: Use when you have a set of seed genes (omic-hits such as frequently mutated genes per cancer type) and a reference interactome, and need a context-specific subnetwork whose recovered nodes can be scored against known drivers (IntOGen).

name: seed-node-network-anchoring
