description: Use when you have omic-hit seed nodes (e.g., mutated or differentially active proteins) and a large reference interactome, and need to shrink it to a context-relevant region before network propagation or edge scoring.

name: segmentation-backend-callable-configuration
description: Use when a spatial transcriptomics pipeline needs cell/nucleus segmentation for images (e.g. the RESOLVE mouse liver example) and the segmentation backend (Cellpose or Baysor) and its parameters must be configured and validated within SPArrOW.

name: segmentation-conflict-resolution-across-patches
description: Use when large images must be segmented patch-wise (e.g., memory limits) and you need to verify that overlapping patches do not introduce boundary conflicts between duplicated cell segmentations.

name: segmentation-labels-layer-generation
description: Use when a raw spatial transcriptomics image (e.g. the RESOLVE mouse liver example) must be converted into a per-cell labels layer before transcript allocation, and a reproducible Cellpose-based segmentation config is needed.

name: segmentation-ratio-computation
description: Use when evaluating whether segmentation of large spatial omics images (e.g. Xenium, MERSCOPE) hits memory/time limits, or when quantifying how much Sopa patching reduces RAM and runtime versus whole-image/whole-transcript segmentation.

name: self-supervised-loss-weighting
description: Use when tuning SSGATE's combined weighted loss on paired transcriptome-proteome data (e.g. BMNC, SLN111_D1) and you need to determine how the balance parameter affects clustering/integration performance at a fixed neighbor count (15).

name: sem-reproducibility-across-network-states
description: Use when validating a dynamical biomolecular network model's stability: you need to show cell fate predictions (e.g., proliferation, apoptosis) are insensitive to small (up to 10%) input perturbations via SEM.

name: semi-synthetic-benchmark-fdr-power-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether a variable-selection or conditional-dependency method controls FDR while gaining power on semi-synthetic single-cell data, especially when comparing hierarchical (group-level) vs. gene-level test resolutions.

name: semi-synthetic-label-perturbation
description: Use when auditing a cell-annotation error detector: you need a ground-truth correct/incorrect flag per cell to compute AUROC, so labels must be synthetically misclassified at controlled fractions.

name: semi-synthetic-single-cell-data-simulation
description: Use when you need ground-truth conditional dependencies to benchmark FDR control and power of feature-selection methods on single-cell data, or to compare importance-score choices (e.g., linear OLS vs MLP) via held-out predictive performance.

name: sensitivity-analysis-vs-imputation-benchmark
description: Use when a LUCID model was fit with integrated imputation on incomplete omics data and you need a sensitivity check comparing complete-case parameter estimates side by side with the imputed-model results.

name: sequencing-depth-correlated-dimension-exclusion
description: Use when processing sci-L3-RNA/ATAC count matrices with Seurat/Signac and cell assignments must be validated against SNV ground truth — deep-sequenced cells otherwise separate on a depth-driven component.

name: seurat-cellcyclescoring-annotation
description: Use when a single-cell experiment co-profiles transcriptome and interaction scores (e.g., scMAPIT-seq cell×gene MAPIT matrix) and cells must be staged by cell-cycle phase before phase-specific correlation or clustering.

name: seurat-multiomics-object-construction
description: Use when a multimodal single-cell dataset is stored as .h5mu/MuData (e.g. PBMC RNA+ATAC) and must be loaded into R as MultiAssayExperiment or Seurat with one assay per modality.

name: seurat-object-construction-from-count-matrices
description: Use when you have sci-L3-RNA and sci-L3-ATAC count matrices plus per-cell depth metrics (e.g. single_cell_summary_all.txt) and need cell objects for PCA/LSI, UMAP, and cell-type assignment against SNV ground truth.

name: seurat-object-manipulation
description: Use when a spatial transcriptomics analysis must be carried out on a Seurat object so that stImage functions (PreProcessing, extractNeighborDist, diagnostic plots) can access its spatial assay and reductions.

name: sgrna-logfc-aggregation
description: Use when multiple CRISPR/Cas9 screening cohorts (e.g. Freeman, Kearney, Manguso, Pan, Patel, Vredevoogd, Lawson) must be combined into a consensus gene ranking of immune-evasion or immunotherapy-response modifiers.

name: shared-feature-subset-correlation-computation
description: Use when integrating factorized program matrices (e.g. cNMF outputs in .h5ad) across datasets with incomplete feature overlap, where program-pair correlations must be computed over shared features before anchoring.

name: shortest-path-naive-network-construction
description: Use when multi-omics perturbation data (transcriptomics, proteomics, phosphoproteomics) must be connected to known receptors/perturbed molecules to yield a context-specific mechanistic signaling network.

name: signaling-network-tool-capability-comparison
description: Use when decision support for choosing a mechanistic signaling-network tool when the analysis goal requires knowing which omics data types (transcriptomics, proteomics, phosphoproteomics, metabolomics) each tool integrates and how its PKN and algorithm differ.

name: significance-star-overlay-on-heatmap
description: Use when you have fold-change and p-value/q-value matrices from multi-omics data (mutations, CNA, methylation, miRNA-mRNA, protein-mRNA) and need a heatmap with overlaid significance markers.

name: silhouette-based-cluster-number-selection
description: Use when running CHAI-AvgSim or CHAI-SNF on scRNAseq data and the true number of clusters is unknown, so highest-ranked_k for Spectral Clustering must be estimated from the integrated similarity matrix.

name: silhouette-based-optimal-k-selection
description: Use when running CHAI-AvgSim or CHAI-SNF on a SingleCellExperiment (e.g., baron_mouse_1) and the true number of clusters is unknown, so a data-driven highest-ranked_k must be selected before Spectral Clustering on the AvgSim_matrix or snf_matrix.

name: silhouette-score-k-selection
description: Use when running CHAI-AvgSim or CHAI-SNF on scRNAseq data where the true number of clusters is unknown and a highest-ranked_k must be selected for Spectral Clustering via silhouette score.

name: similarity-network-fusion-of-binary-matrices
description: Use when you have cluster assignments (or an extra omics similarity matrix, e.g. spatial-coordinate KNN) from multiple scRNAseq clustering methods and need a single fused similarity matrix for consensus cell-type identification.

name: simulated-ground-truth-fidelity-scoring
description: Use when you have simulated scRNA-seq/SRT datasets with known ground-truth annotations (groups, DEGs, batches, trajectory) and need to rank simulation methods by a functionality score.

name: simulated-pangenome-phenotype-generation
description: Use when benchmarking whether a gene-trait association tool recovers a simulated causal gene from continuous numeric phenotypes, varying isolate count (25–200) and effect size (σ), with the causal gene's rank as the metric.

name: simulated-read-variant-calling-validation
description: Use when simulated sequencing reads have been generated with an injected pathogenic variant and the dataset must be certified for educational variant-calling exercises before release to students.

name: simulated-rnaseq-ground-truth-validation
description: Use when simulated RNA-seq FASTQ reads (Polyester-generated with a known DE ground truth) must be checked that quantification, DESeq2 testing, and GO enrichment reproduce the injected signal before release as a teaching dataset.

name: simulation-estimation-bias-assessment
description: Use when you must quantify estimation bias for LUCID (exposures G, omics Z, outcome Y) under sporadic, completely-at-random missing omics entries — e.g., complete-case analysis is infeasible and you need to compare integrated imputation vs. mean imputation against known ground truth.

name: simulation-execution-time-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking how execution time and memory consumption of scRNA-seq/SRT simulators (e.g., dyntoy, SRTsim, scDesign, scDesign2, scDesign3, ZINB-WaVE) scale with cell or gene numbers.

name: simulation-fidelity-metric-computation
description: Use when you have a real reference scRNA-seq/SRT expression matrix plus simulated counterpart matrices and need quantitative accuracy scores of simulation fidelity across data properties.

name: simulation-method-accuracy-score-wrangling
description: Use when a benchmark table contains paired per-method accuracy scores for two transcriptomics modalities (SRT vs scRNA-seq) and you need to test whether method rankings or scores transfer between them.

name: simulation-replicate-aggregation
description: Use when comparing clustering methods on single-cell multi-omics data (e.g. CITE-seq or SMAGE-seq) that lack true spatial coordinates, and you need replicated simulated-2D-grid benchmarks with AMI/NMI/ARI summaries.

name: single-cell-atac-lsi-dimensionality-reduction
